"""Document conformance inside Procedure Studio: schema packages, validation, BREX, rule sets, stylesheets.

The schema layer (``registry``, ``identify``, ``validation``, ``brex``, ``security``, ``schema``) comes
from ASTHRA's validation core, without SGML and without ASTHRA's document store. ``rules`` and
``stylesheets`` are Studio's own. ``service.Conformance`` is the one entry point the rest of Studio uses.
"""



================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\conformance\rules.py
================================================================================

"""Project rule sets: business rules beyond the schema, added by the publication team.

Two formats, both installed into the rule library (``<data>/conformance/rules``) and checked in the
business-rules stage next to the S1000D BREX:

* **Schematron** (ISO, ``.sch``): ``assert``/``report`` with ``@id`` (rule id) and ``@role``
  (``fatal | error | warning | info``). Run through lxml's ISO Schematron implementation.
* **Rule file** (``.yaml``/``.yml``/``.json``): a list of XPath rules, for teams that do not write
  Schematron. Each rule has an ``id``, a ``context`` XPath and one test:

  .. code-block:: yaml

     id: acme-house-rules
     name: ACME house rules
     applies_to: {standards: [S1000D], doc_types: [proced], roots: [dmodule]}   # all optional
     namespaces: {}                                   # prefix -> URI, for namespaced documents
     rules:
       - id: ACME-001
         severity: error                              # fatal | error | warning | info (default error)
         context: //proceduralStep
         assert: "normalize-space(para) != ''"        # must be true for every context node
         message: Every procedural step has text.
         suggestion: Write the instruction in the step's para.
       - id: ACME-002
         context: //para
         forbid: "contains(., ';')"                   # must be false
         message: Do not use semicolons.
       - id: ACME-003
         context: //dmCode
         attribute: modelIdentCode                    # check an attribute (or the text when omitted)
         allowed: [TECHPUB, SLSBSELV]                 # value list ...
       - id: ACME-004
         context: //quantityValue
         pattern: '^\\d+(\\.\\d+)?$'                  # ... or a regular expression (full match)
         message: Quantities are plain decimal numbers.

Every rule set can be enabled or disabled, and limited to standards, document types or root
elements. A rule that cannot be evaluated is reported as not checked, never as passed.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from lxml import etree

from .security.xml_safe import document_parser
from .validation.model import Diagnostic, Severity

SEVERITIES = {s.value for s in Severity}
SVRL = "{http://purl.oclc.org/dsdl/svrl}"


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def _slug(s: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "-", s).strip("-").lower() or "rules"


@dataclass
class Applies:
    standards: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    doc_types: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    roots: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @classmethod
    def of(cls, d: dict | None) -> "Applies":
        d = d or {}
        lst = lambda v: [v] if isinstance(v, str) else list(v or [])
        return cls([s.upper() for s in lst(d.get("standards") or d.get("standard"))],
                   lst(d.get("doc_types") or d.get("doc_type")), lst(d.get("roots") or d.get("root")))

    def fits(self, standard: str | None, doc_type: str | None, root: str | None) -> bool:
        return ((not self.standards or (standard or "").upper() in self.standards)
                and (not self.doc_types or doc_type in self.doc_types)
                and (not self.roots or root in self.roots))

    def as_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {"standards": self.standards, "doc_types": self.doc_types, "roots": self.roots}


@dataclass
class Outcome:
    diagnostics: list[Diagnostic] = field(default_factory=list)
    checked: int = 0
    not_checked: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)     # (rule id, reason)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- XPath rule files
def _line(node, root) -> tuple[int | None, etree._Element | None]:
    el = node.getparent() if isinstance(node, etree._ElementUnicodeResult) else node
    if not isinstance(el, etree._Element):
        el = root
    return el.sourceline, el


def parse_rule_file(data: bytes, name: str) -> dict:
    text = data.decode("utf-8-sig")
    if name.lower().endswith(".json"):
        doc = json.loads(text)
    else:
        import yaml
        doc = yaml.safe_load(text)
    if isinstance(doc, list):
        doc = {"rules": doc}
    if not isinstance(doc, dict) or not isinstance(doc.get("rules"), list) or not doc["rules"]:
        raise ValueError("a rule file needs a non-empty 'rules' list")
    ns = doc.get("namespaces") or {}
    for i, r in enumerate(doc["rules"], start=1):
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            raise ValueError(f"rule {i} is not a mapping")
        r.setdefault("id", f"RULE-{i:03d}")
        if not r.get("context"):
            raise ValueError(f"{r['id']}: 'context' (an XPath) is required")
        tests = [k for k in ("assert", "forbid", "allowed", "pattern") if k in r]
        if len(tests) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{r['id']}: give exactly one of assert, forbid, allowed, pattern")
        sev = str(r.get("severity", "error")).lower()
        if sev not in SEVERITIES:
            raise ValueError(f"{r['id']}: severity must be one of {', '.join(sorted(SEVERITIES))}")
        r["severity"] = sev
        try:                                              # compile now, so a bad rule fails at install
            etree.XPath(r["context"], namespaces=ns)
            for k in ("assert", "forbid"):
                if k in r:
                    etree.XPath(r[k], namespaces=ns)
            if "pattern" in r:
                re.compile(r["pattern"])
        except (etree.XPathSyntaxError, re.error) as e:
            raise ValueError(f"{r['id']}: {e}") from e
    return doc


def check_rule_file(doc: dict, tree, set_name: str, file: str) -> Outcome:
    out = Outcome()
    root = tree.getroot() if hasattr(tree, "getroot") else tree
    ns = doc.get("namespaces") or {}
    for r in doc["rules"]:
        try:
            nodes = etree.XPath(r["context"], namespaces=ns)(root)
        except etree.XPathError as e:
            out.not_checked.append((r["id"], str(e)))
            continue
        out.checked += 1
        nodes = nodes if isinstance(nodes, list) else []
        for n in nodes:
            ok, value = True, None
            try:
                if "assert" in r:
                    ok = bool(etree.XPath(r["assert"], namespaces=ns)(n))
                elif "forbid" in r:
                    ok = not bool(etree.XPath(r["forbid"], namespaces=ns)(n))
                else:
                    el = n if isinstance(n, etree._Element) else None
                    if r.get("attribute"):
                        if el is None or el.get(r["attribute"]) is None:
                            continue                      # absent attribute: a schema matter, not this rule's
                        value = el.get(r["attribute"])
                    else:
                        value = ("".join(el.itertext()) if el is not None else str(n)).strip()
                    if "allowed" in r:
                        ok = value in [str(v) for v in r["allowed"]]
                    else:
                        ok = re.fullmatch(r["pattern"], value) is not None
            except etree.XPathError as e:
                out.not_checked.append((r["id"], str(e)))
                break
            if ok:
                continue
            line, el = _line(n, root)
            from .validation.pipeline import readable_path
            msg = r.get("message") or f"Rule {r['id']} is not met."
            if value is not None:
                msg += f" Found '{value}'" + (f" in @{r['attribute']}." if r.get("attribute") else ".")
            out.diagnostics.append(Diagnostic(
                stage=4, severity=r["severity"], rule_id=str(r["id"]), category="business-rule", message=msg,
                suggestion=r.get("suggestion") or (f"Allowed: {', '.join(map(str, r['allowed']))}." if "allowed" in r else None),
                source_file=file, line=line, element_path=readable_path(el) if el is not None else None,
                attribute=r.get("attribute"), value=value, reference=f"Rule set {set_name}"))
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Schematron
def compile_schematron(data: bytes):
    from lxml import isoschematron
    try:
        doc = etree.fromstring(data, document_parser())
    except etree.XMLSyntaxError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"the Schematron file is not well-formed: {e}") from e
    try:
        return isoschematron.Schematron(doc, store_report=True), doc
    except etree.SchematronParseError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"not a valid ISO Schematron schema: {e}") from e
    except etree.XSLTParseError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"the Schematron could not be compiled: {e}") from e


def check_schematron(compiled, sch_doc, tree, set_name: str, file: str) -> Outcome:
    from .validation.pipeline import readable_path
    out = Outcome()
    compiled.validate(tree)
    report = compiled.validation_report
    sch_ns = "{http://purl.oclc.org/dsdl/schematron}"
    roles = {a.get("id"): (a.get("role") or "error").lower() for a in sch_doc.iter(f"{sch_ns}assert", f"{sch_ns}report") if a.get("id")}
    out.checked = sum(1 for _ in sch_doc.iter(f"{sch_ns}assert", f"{sch_ns}report"))
    root = tree.getroot()
    for i, f in enumerate(report.iter(f"{SVRL}failed-assert", f"{SVRL}successful-report"), start=1):
        rid = f.get("id") or f"SCH-{i:03d}"
        role = (f.get("role") or roles.get(f.get("id")) or "error").lower()
        if role not in SEVERITIES:
            role = "warning" if role in ("warn", "caution") else "error"
        text = " ".join(" ".join("".join(t.itertext()).split()) for t in f.iter(f"{SVRL}text")) or f.get("test", "")
        el = None
        try:
            hit = root.getroottree().xpath(f.get("location") or "")
            el = hit[0] if hit and isinstance(hit[0], etree._Element) else None
        except etree.XPathError:
            pass
        out.diagnostics.append(Diagnostic(
            stage=4, severity=role, rule_id=rid, category="business-rule", message=text,
            suggestion=None, source_file=file, line=el.sourceline if el is not None else None,
            element_path=readable_path(el) if el is not None else f.get("location"),
            raw_message=f.get("test"), reference=f"Schematron {set_name}"))
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- library
class RuleLibrary:
    """Installed rule sets: ``index.json`` plus the files, one folder."""

    def __init__(self, root: Path):
        self.root = Path(root)
        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.index_file = self.root / "index.json"
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._compiled: dict[str, tuple[float, object]] = {}

    def list(self) -> list[dict]:
        try:
            return json.loads(self.index_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            return []

    def _save(self, entries: list[dict]) -> None:
        self.index_file.write_text(json.dumps(entries, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    def get(self, rid: str) -> dict:
        e = next((x for x in self.list() if x["id"] == rid), None)
        if e is None:
            raise KeyError(f"no rule set {rid}")
        return e

    def install(self, data: bytes, filename: str, name: str | None = None, applies_to: dict | None = None) -> dict:
        """Add or replace a rule set (same id replaces). Raises ValueError for a file that does not compile."""
        low = filename.lower()
        if low.endswith((".sch", ".schematron")):
            _, doc = compile_schematron(data)
            sch = "{http://purl.oclc.org/dsdl/schematron}"
            title = doc.findtext(f"{sch}title") or Path(filename).stem
            kind, count, rid = "schematron", sum(1 for _ in doc.iter(f"{sch}assert", f"{sch}report")), _slug(Path(filename).stem)
            ext, app = ".sch", Applies.of(applies_to)
        elif low.endswith((".yaml", ".yml", ".json")):
            doc = parse_rule_file(data, filename)
            title = doc.get("name") or Path(filename).stem
            kind, count, rid = "xpath", len(doc["rules"]), _slug(doc.get("id") or Path(filename).stem)
            ext, app = Path(low).suffix, Applies.of(applies_to or doc.get("applies_to"))
        else:
            raise ValueError("a rule set is a Schematron file (.sch) or a rule file (.yaml, .yml, .json)")
        with self._lock:
            entries = [e for e in self.list() if e["id"] != rid]
            old = next((e for e in self.list() if e["id"] == rid), None)
            file = rid + ext
            (self.root / file).write_bytes(data)
            entry = {"id": rid, "name": name or title, "kind": kind, "file": file, "rules": count,
                     "applies_to": app.as_dict(), "enabled": old["enabled"] if old else True,
                     "source_name": filename, "installed_at": _now()}
            entries.append(entry)
            self._save(sorted(entries, key=lambda e: e["id"]))
            self._compiled.pop(rid, None)
        return entry

    def update(self, rid: str, enabled: bool | None = None, applies_to: dict | None = None, name: str | None = None) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            entries = self.list()
            e = next((x for x in entries if x["id"] == rid), None)
            if e is None:
                raise KeyError(f"no rule set {rid}")
            if enabled is not None:
                e["enabled"] = bool(enabled)
            if applies_to is not None:
                e["applies_to"] = Applies.of(applies_to).as_dict()
            if name:
                e["name"] = name
            self._save(entries)
            return e

    def remove(self, rid: str) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            entries = self.list()
            e = next((x for x in entries if x["id"] == rid), None)
            if e is None:
                raise KeyError(f"no rule set {rid}")
            (self.root / e["file"]).unlink(missing_ok=True)
            self._save([x for x in entries if x["id"] != rid])
            self._compiled.pop(rid, None)

    def source(self, rid: str) -> tuple[str, bytes]:
        e = self.get(rid)
        return e["file"], (self.root / e["file"]).read_bytes()

    def _load(self, e: dict):
        p = self.root / e["file"]
        mtime = p.stat().st_mtime
        hit = self._compiled.get(e["id"])
        if hit and hit[0] == mtime:
            return hit[1]
        data = p.read_bytes()
        obj = compile_schematron(data) if e["kind"] == "schematron" else parse_rule_file(data, e["file"])
        self._compiled[e["id"]] = (mtime, obj)
        return obj

    def applicable(self, standard: str | None, doc_type: str | None, root: str | None) -> list[dict]:
        return [e for e in self.list() if e.get("enabled", True)
                and Applies.of(e.get("applies_to")).fits(standard, doc_type, root)]

    def check(self, tree, standard: str | None, doc_type: str | None, file: str) -> tuple[Outcome, list[dict]]:
        root = etree.QName(tree.getroot()).localname
        total, used = Outcome(), self.applicable(standard, doc_type, root)
        for e in used:
            try:
                obj = self._load(e)
                o = check_schematron(*obj, tree, e["name"], file) if e["kind"] == "schematron" \
                    else check_rule_file(obj, tree, e["name"], file)
            except Exception as ex:                       # noqa: BLE001 - one broken set never hides the others
                total.not_checked.append((e["id"], f"rule set could not run: {ex}"))
                continue
            total.diagnostics += o.diagnostics
            total.checked += o.checked
            total.not_checked += o.not_checked
        return total, used



================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\conformance\service.py
================================================================================

"""One entry point for checking documents: identify -> validate (schema) -> business rules (BREX + rule sets).

    conf = Conformance(data_dir / "conformance")
    report = conf.check(xml_bytes, "DMC-....XML", prefer="s1000d/4.2/acme:proced")
    html, used = conf.view(xml_bytes)

Reports are plain dicts (JSON-ready). Nothing here reaches the network.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import shutil
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from lxml import etree

from .brex.library import BrexLibrary
from .identify.service import identify, parse_xml, sniff
from .registry import installer
from .registry.builder import BuildError
from .registry.service import RegistryError, SchemaRegistry
from .rules import RuleLibrary
from .storage.db import Database
from .stylesheets import StylesheetLibrary
from .validation.diagnostics import finalize
from .validation.model import Diagnostic, Severity, Stage, StageResult, Status
from .validation.pipeline import brex_stage, validate_bytes

# What Studio generates, and which document types can validate it (for status and schema choice)
TARGETS = {
    "s1000d_proced": {"label": "S1000D procedure (530, 710)", "standard": "S1000D", "roots": ["dmodule"], "doc_types": ["proced"]},
    "s1000d_ipd": {"label": "S1000D IPD (941)", "standard": "S1000D", "roots": ["dmodule"], "doc_types": ["ipd"]},
    "ata_cmm": {"label": "ATA iSpec 2200 CMM", "standard": "ATA2200", "roots": ["cmm"], "doc_types": ["cmm"]},
}


class Conformance:
    def __init__(self, root: Path):
        self.root = Path(root)
        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.db = Database(self.root / "registry.sqlite3")
        self.registry = SchemaRegistry(self.db, self.root / "packages")
        self.brex = BrexLibrary(self.root / "brex")
        self.registry.brex = self.brex
        self.rules = RuleLibrary(self.root / "rules")
        self.styles = StylesheetLibrary(self.root / "stylesheets")
        self.staging = self.root / "staging"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ status
    def coverage(self) -> dict:
        """For each Studio output: the installed document types that can validate it."""
        out = {}
        for key, t in TARGETS.items():
            hits = []
            for p in self.registry.list(include_disabled=False):
                if p.manifest.standard != t["standard"]:
                    continue
                for dt in p.manifest.doc_types:
                    if dt.match.local_name in t["roots"] and (dt.id in t["doc_types"] or dt.content_family in
                                                              ("procedure" if key == "s1000d_proced" else "ipd", "other")):
                        hits.append({"package_id": p.manifest.key, "doc_type": dt.id, "label": f"{p.manifest.name} · {dt.label}",
                                     "provenance": p.manifest.provenance})
            out[key] = {"label": t["label"], "options": hits}
        return out

    def status(self) -> dict:
        return {"packages": [p.summary() | {"path": None} for p in self.registry.list()],
                "brex": self.brex.list(), "brex_substitutes": self.brex.substitutes(),
                "rules": self.rules.list(), "stylesheets": self.styles.list(), "coverage": self.coverage()}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ schema packages
    def inspect_upload(self, files: list[tuple[str, bytes]]) -> dict:
        """Stage an upload (a zip, or the files of a folder with their relative paths) and say what it holds."""
        sid, src = installer.new_staging(self.staging)
        for rel, data in files:
            rel = rel.replace("\\", "/").lstrip("/")
            if rel.lower().endswith(".zip") and len(files) == 1:
                zp = src.parent / "upload.zip"
                zp.write_bytes(data)
                from .security.paths import safe_extract_zip
                safe_extract_zip(zp, src)
                zp.unlink()
                continue
            if not installer.wanted(rel, len(data)):
                continue
            from .security.paths import confine
            dst = confine(src, rel)
            dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            dst.write_bytes(data)
        try:
            proposal = installer.inspect(src)
        except BuildError as e:
            shutil.rmtree(src.parent, ignore_errors=True)
            raise ValueError(str(e)) from e
        return {"staging": sid, **proposal}

    def install_staged(self, sid: str, choice: dict, replace: bool = False) -> dict:
        src = (self.staging / sid / "src")
        if not src.is_dir():
            raise ValueError("this upload has expired; add the schemas again")
        try:
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
                built = installer.build(src, choice, Path(tmp) / "package.zip")
                try:
                    pkg = self.registry.replace(built) if replace else self.registry.install(built)
                except RegistryError as e:
                    if not replace and "already installed" in str(e):
                        raise ValueError(f"{e}. Choose “Replace” to install this build over it.") from e
                    raise ValueError(str(e)) from e
            brex = []
            if choice.get("kind") == "s1000d":
                brex = installer.install_brex_found(src, self.brex, choice.get("issue"))
            return {"package": pkg.summary(), "brex_installed": brex}
        except BuildError as e:
            raise ValueError(str(e)) from e
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(self.staging / sid, ignore_errors=True)

    def install_package_dir(self, path: Path) -> dict:
        """Install a ready-made package folder or zip (used for the evaluation packages and by tests)."""
        try:
            return self.registry.install(Path(path)).summary()
        except RegistryError as e:
            raise ValueError(str(e)) from e

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ checking
    def check(self, data: bytes, file: str, prefer: str | None = None, standard_hint: str | None = None) -> dict:
        """Full check of one document. ``prefer`` = "package_id:doc_type" to use when the document's own
        declaration does not decide (Studio's per-output schema choice)."""
        sn = sniff(data)
        tree0, _ = parse_xml(data)
        root0 = tree0.getroot() if tree0 is not None else None
        packages = [p for p in self.registry.list(include_disabled=False)]
        ident = identify(root0, packages, sn, data)
        pkg_id = dt_id = None
        how = None
        pref = tuple(prefer.split(":", 1)) if prefer and ":" in prefer else None
        if ident.chosen:
            pkg_id, dt_id, how = ident.chosen.package_id, ident.chosen.doc_type, "declared by the document"
            if pref and pref != (pkg_id, dt_id) and any((c.package_id, c.doc_type) == pref for c in ident.compatible):
                pkg_id, dt_id, how = pref[0], pref[1], "chosen for this output"
        elif pref and any((c.package_id, c.doc_type) == pref for c in ident.candidates + ident.compatible):
            pkg_id, dt_id, how = pref[0], pref[1], "chosen for this output"
        elif ident.status == "needs-choice" and len(ident.compatible) == 1:
            c = ident.compatible[0]
            pkg_id, dt_id, how = c.package_id, c.doc_type, "the only installed schema that fits"
        rep, tree = validate_bytes(data, file, self.registry, pkg_id, dt_id)
        standard = next((p.manifest.standard for p in packages if p.manifest.key == pkg_id), None) or standard_hint
        if standard is None and root0 is not None:
            standard = {"dmodule": "S1000D", "pm": "S1000D", "cmm": "ATA2200"}.get(etree.QName(root0).localname)
        self._business_rules(tree, rep, file, pkg_id, dt_id, standard)
        finalize(rep)
        for d in rep.diagnostics:                         # keep the rule-set category after finalize
            if d.stage == Stage.BUSINESS_RULES:
                d.category = d.category if d.category in ("brex-missing", "brex-substitute", "brex-issue", "brex-not-checked") \
                    else "business-rule"
        res = {"file": file, "identification": {**ident.as_dict(), "package_id": pkg_id, "doc_type": dt_id,
                                                 "standard": standard, "how": how},
               "statuses": rep.statuses(), "counts": rep.counts(),
               "stages": [{"stage": int(s.stage), "name": STAGE_NAMES.get(int(s.stage), str(s.stage)),
                           "status": s.status.value, "note": s.note} for s in sorted(rep.stages, key=lambda s: s.stage)],
               "diagnostics": [d.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True) for d in rep.diagnostics],
               "entities": rep.entities}
        res["passed"] = res["statuses"]["structural"] == "passed" and res["counts"]["error"] + res["counts"]["fatal"] == 0
        return res

    def _business_rules(self, tree, rep, file: str, pkg_id, dt_id, standard) -> None:
        if tree is None:
            if not any(s.stage == Stage.BUSINESS_RULES for s in rep.stages):
                rep.stages.append(StageResult(stage=Stage.BUSINESS_RULES, status=Status.NOT_RUN, note="document could not be read"))
            return
        rep.stages = [s for s in rep.stages if s.stage != Stage.BUSINESS_RULES]
        notes, failed, ran = [], False, False
        if (standard or "").upper() == "S1000D" and pkg_id:
            try:
                _, pkg, dt = self.registry.schema_for(pkg_id, dt_id)
                before = len(rep.stages)
                brex_stage(tree, self.brex, pkg, dt, file, rep)
                st = rep.stages.pop() if len(rep.stages) > before else None
                if st is not None:
                    notes.append("BREX: " + st.note)
                    ran = ran or st.status in (Status.PASSED, Status.FAILED)
                    failed = failed or st.status == Status.FAILED
            except RegistryError as e:
                notes.append(f"BREX not checked: {e}")
        root = etree.QName(tree.getroot()).localname
        outcome, used = self.rules.check(tree, standard, dt_id, file)
        if used:
            ran = True
            rep.diagnostics += outcome.diagnostics
            failed = failed or any(d.severity in (Severity.ERROR, Severity.FATAL) for d in outcome.diagnostics)
            notes.append(f"rule sets: {', '.join(e['name'] for e in used)} ({outcome.checked} rules checked)")
        for rid, why in outcome.not_checked:
            rep.diagnostics.append(Diagnostic(stage=Stage.BUSINESS_RULES, severity=Severity.WARNING, rule_id="VAL-RULE-NOT-CHECKED",
                                              category="rule-not-checked", source_file=file,
                                              message=f"Rule {rid} could not be evaluated and was NOT checked: {why}"))
        if not ran and not notes:
            notes.append(f"no BREX or rule set applies to <{root}>")
        rep.stages.append(StageResult(stage=Stage.BUSINESS_RULES,
                                      status=Status.FAILED if failed else Status.PASSED if ran else Status.NOT_RUN,
                                      note="; ".join(notes)))

    def view(self, data: bytes, stylesheet: str | None = None, standard: str | None = None, doc_type: str | None = None) -> dict:
        from .security.xml_safe import document_parser
        try:
            tree = etree.parse(io.BytesIO(data), document_parser())
        except etree.XMLSyntaxError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"the document is not well-formed XML: {e}") from e
        if standard is None:
            standard = {"dmodule": "S1000D", "pm": "S1000D", "cmm": "ATA2200"}.get(etree.QName(tree.getroot()).localname)
        html, used = self.styles.view(tree, standard, doc_type, stylesheet)
        return {"html": html, "stylesheet": used and {k: used[k] for k in ("id", "name", "builtin")}}

    def transform(self, data: bytes, standard: str | None, doc_type: str | None) -> tuple[bytes, list[dict]]:
        from .security.xml_safe import document_parser
        try:
            root = etree.QName(etree.fromstring(data, document_parser()).tag).localname
        except etree.XMLSyntaxError:
            return data, []                                # not XML: nothing to transform; the check reports why
        return self.styles.transform(data, standard, doc_type, root)


STAGE_NAMES = {1: "Integrity", 2: "Well-formed XML", 3: "Schema", 4: "Business rules", 5: "References"}



================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\conformance\stylesheets.py

"""XSLT stylesheets: how documents are shown, and optional transforms applied before validation.

Two kinds:

* ``view``       XML -> HTML, for reading a document in the Check screen (and for review exports).
                 Built-in views cover S1000D data modules and the ATA CMM; an installed view for the same
                 documents takes precedence over the built-in one.
* ``transform``  XML -> XML, applied to Studio's output before it is validated and published: house
                 conventions, a customer's flavour of the standard, added boilerplate. Transforms run in
                 ``order`` and only on the documents they apply to.

A stylesheet is a single ``.xsl``/``.xslt`` file, or a ``.zip`` with the main stylesheet and the files it
includes or imports. Stylesheets cannot reach the network or write files; includes are confined to the
stylesheet's own folder. XSLT 1.0 (libxslt).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import re
import shutil
import threading
import zipfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from lxml import etree

from .rules import Applies
from .security.paths import PathViolation, safe_extract_zip
from .security.xml_safe import ConfinedResolver, document_parser

BUILTIN_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "builtin" / "stylesheets"
BUILTINS = [
    {"id": "builtin-s1000d-view", "name": "S1000D reading view", "kind": "view", "file": "s1000d-view.xsl",
     "applies_to": {"standards": ["S1000D"], "doc_types": [], "roots": ["dmodule"]}},
    {"id": "builtin-ata-cmm-view", "name": "ATA CMM reading view", "kind": "view", "file": "ata-cmm-view.xsl",
     "applies_to": {"standards": ["ATA2200"], "doc_types": [], "roots": ["cmm"]}},
]
XSL = "{http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform}"


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def _slug(s: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "-", s).strip("-").lower() or "stylesheet"


ACCESS = etree.XSLTAccessControl(read_file=True, write_file=False, create_dir=False,
                                 read_network=False, write_network=False)


def compile_xslt(path: Path) -> etree.XSLT:
    parser = document_parser()
    parser.resolvers.add(ConfinedResolver([path.parent]))
    try:
        doc = etree.parse(str(path), parser)
    except etree.XMLSyntaxError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"the stylesheet is not well-formed XML: {e}") from e
    if doc.getroot().tag not in (f"{XSL}stylesheet", f"{XSL}transform"):
        raise ValueError("not an XSLT stylesheet (root must be xsl:stylesheet or xsl:transform)")
    try:
        return etree.XSLT(doc, access_control=ACCESS)
    except etree.XSLTParseError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"the stylesheet does not compile: {e}") from e


class StylesheetLibrary:
    def __init__(self, root: Path):
        self.root = Path(root)
        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.index_file = self.root / "index.json"
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._compiled: dict[str, tuple[float, etree.XSLT]] = {}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ index
    def _installed(self) -> list[dict]:
        try:
            return json.loads(self.index_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            return []

    def _save(self, entries: list[dict]) -> None:
        self.index_file.write_text(json.dumps(entries, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    def _builtin_state(self) -> dict:
        p = self.root / "builtin-state.json"
        try:
            return json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            return {}

    def list(self) -> list[dict]:
        state = self._builtin_state()
        out = [{**b, "builtin": True, "enabled": state.get(b["id"], True), "order": 0} for b in BUILTINS]
        return out + [{**e, "builtin": False} for e in self._installed()]

    def get(self, sid: str) -> dict:
        e = next((x for x in self.list() if x["id"] == sid), None)
        if e is None:
            raise KeyError(f"no stylesheet {sid}")
        return e

    def _path(self, e: dict) -> Path:
        return BUILTIN_DIR / e["file"] if e.get("builtin") else self.root / e["id"] / e["file"]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ install / change
    def install(self, data: bytes, filename: str, kind: str, name: str | None = None,
                applies_to: dict | None = None, order: int = 100, main: str | None = None) -> dict:
        if kind not in ("view", "transform"):
            raise ValueError("kind must be 'view' or 'transform'")
        sid = _slug(Path(filename).stem)
        if any(b["id"] == sid for b in BUILTINS):
            sid += "-custom"
        dest = self.root / sid
        tmp = self.root / f".{sid}.new"
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
        tmp.mkdir(parents=True)
        try:
            if filename.lower().endswith(".zip"):
                zp = tmp / "upload.zip"
                zp.write_bytes(data)
                try:
                    safe_extract_zip(zp, tmp)
                except PathViolation as e:
                    raise ValueError(f"unsafe archive rejected: {e}") from e
                zp.unlink()
                cands = sorted(p for p in tmp.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in (".xsl", ".xslt"))
                if main:
                    cands = [p for p in cands if p.relative_to(tmp).as_posix() == main]
                if not cands:
                    raise ValueError("no .xsl/.xslt stylesheet in the archive" + (f" named {main}" if main else ""))
                # the main stylesheet is the one no other stylesheet includes or imports
                included = {Path(h.get("href", "")).name for p in cands for h in
                            etree.parse(str(p), document_parser()).getroot().iter(f"{XSL}include", f"{XSL}import")}
                roots = [p for p in cands if p.name not in included] or cands
                file = roots[0].relative_to(tmp).as_posix()
            elif filename.lower().endswith((".xsl", ".xslt")):
                file = Path(filename).name
                (tmp / file).write_bytes(data)
            else:
                raise ValueError("a stylesheet is an .xsl/.xslt file, or a .zip with the stylesheet and its includes")
            compile_xslt(tmp / file)                      # must compile before it is accepted
            title = name or Path(file).stem.replace("-", " ").replace("_", " ")
            with self._lock:
                shutil.rmtree(dest, ignore_errors=True)
                tmp.rename(dest)
                entries = [e for e in self._installed() if e["id"] != sid]
                entry = {"id": sid, "name": title, "kind": kind, "file": file, "applies_to": Applies.of(applies_to).as_dict(),
                         "enabled": True, "order": int(order), "source_name": filename, "installed_at": _now()}
                entries.append(entry)
                self._save(sorted(entries, key=lambda e: (e["kind"], e["order"], e["id"])))
                self._compiled.pop(sid, None)
            return {**entry, "builtin": False}
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def update(self, sid: str, enabled: bool | None = None, applies_to: dict | None = None,
               order: int | None = None, name: str | None = None) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            if any(b["id"] == sid for b in BUILTINS):
                if enabled is not None:
                    st = self._builtin_state()
                    st[sid] = bool(enabled)
                    (self.root / "builtin-state.json").write_text(json.dumps(st), encoding="utf-8")
                return next(x for x in self.list() if x["id"] == sid)
            entries = self._installed()
            e = next((x for x in entries if x["id"] == sid), None)
            if e is None:
                raise KeyError(f"no stylesheet {sid}")
            if enabled is not None:
                e["enabled"] = bool(enabled)
            if applies_to is not None:
                e["applies_to"] = Applies.of(applies_to).as_dict()
            if order is not None:
                e["order"] = int(order)
            if name:
                e["name"] = name
            self._save(entries)
            return {**e, "builtin": False}

    def remove(self, sid: str) -> None:
        if any(b["id"] == sid for b in BUILTINS):
            raise ValueError("built-in stylesheets cannot be removed; disable them instead")
        with self._lock:
            entries = self._installed()
            if not any(e["id"] == sid for e in entries):
                raise KeyError(f"no stylesheet {sid}")
            shutil.rmtree(self.root / sid, ignore_errors=True)
            self._save([e for e in entries if e["id"] != sid])
            self._compiled.pop(sid, None)

    def source(self, sid: str) -> tuple[str, bytes]:
        e = self.get(sid)
        p = self._path(e)
        if e.get("builtin") or p.parent == self.root / sid and len(list(p.parent.rglob("*"))) == 1:
            return p.name, p.read_bytes()
        buf = io.BytesIO()                               # several files: give the folder back as a zip
        with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
            for f in (self.root / sid).rglob("*"):
                if f.is_file():
                    z.write(f, f.relative_to(self.root / sid).as_posix())
        return f"{sid}.zip", buf.getvalue()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ use
    def _xslt(self, e: dict) -> etree.XSLT:
        p = self._path(e)
        mtime = p.stat().st_mtime
        hit = self._compiled.get(e["id"])
        if hit and hit[0] == mtime:
            return hit[1]
        x = compile_xslt(p)
        self._compiled[e["id"]] = (mtime, x)
        return x

    def applicable(self, kind: str, standard: str | None, doc_type: str | None, root: str | None) -> list[dict]:
        hits = [e for e in self.list() if e["kind"] == kind and e.get("enabled", True)
                and Applies.of(e.get("applies_to")).fits(standard, doc_type, root)]
        # installed before built-in, then by order
        return sorted(hits, key=lambda e: (e.get("builtin", False), e.get("order", 100), e["id"]))

    def view(self, tree, standard: str | None, doc_type: str | None, stylesheet: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, dict | None]:
        """HTML for a document. -> (html, stylesheet entry used or None)."""
        root = etree.QName(tree.getroot()).localname
        if stylesheet:
            e = self.get(stylesheet)
        else:
            cands = self.applicable("view", standard, doc_type, root)
            e = cands[0] if cands else None
        if e is None:
            return generic_view(tree), None
        try:
            res = self._xslt(e)(tree)
        except etree.XSLTApplyError as ex:
            raise ValueError(f"{e['name']} failed on this document: {ex}") from ex
        return etree.tostring(res, method="html", encoding="unicode") if res.getroot() is not None else str(res), e

    def transform(self, data: bytes, standard: str | None, doc_type: str | None, root: str | None) -> tuple[bytes, list[dict]]:
        """Apply every enabled transform that fits, in order. -> (new bytes, entries applied)."""
        used = self.applicable("transform", standard, doc_type, root)
        if not used:
            return data, []
        tree = etree.parse(io.BytesIO(data), document_parser())
        for e in used:
            try:
                tree = self._xslt(e)(tree)
            except etree.XSLTApplyError as ex:
                raise ValueError(f"transform {e['name']} failed: {ex}") from ex
            if tree.getroot() is None:
                raise ValueError(f"transform {e['name']} produced no XML document")
        out = etree.tostring(tree, xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8", pretty_print=True)
        return out, used


def generic_view(tree) -> str:
    """Fallback when no view fits: the document as an indented outline."""
    from html import escape
    lines = []

    def walk(el, depth):
        if not isinstance(el.tag, str):
            return
        attrs = " ".join(f'{etree.QName(k).localname}="{escape(v)}"' for k, v in el.attrib.items()
                         if not k.startswith("{http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance}"))
        text = (el.text or "").strip()
        lines.append(f'<div style="margin-left:{depth}em"><b>{escape(etree.QName(el).localname)}</b>'
                     f'{" <small>" + attrs + "</small>" if attrs else ""}{" — " + escape(text) if text else ""}</div>')
        for c in el:
            walk(c, depth + 1)
    walk(tree.getroot(), 0)
    return ('<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>body{font:13px/1.5 system-ui,sans-serif;padding:1rem 1.5rem;color:#18212b}'
            'small{color:#6f7a86}</style></head><body><p><i>No view stylesheet fits this document; showing its structure.</i></p>'
            + "".join(lines) + "</body></html>")

"""Checking a document against BREX rules.

Rule semantics (S1000D allowedObjectFlag):
  0  prohibited  — whatever the path finds is a violation (with object values: only those values are prohibited)
  1  required    — the path must find something
  2  allowed     — whatever the path finds must have one of the listed values (no values: no restriction)
Paths are XPath. Most run on lxml (fast) with the XPath 2.0 functions BREX files use added per
expression; anything lxml cannot evaluate falls back to elementpath (full XPath 2.0). A rule that
neither can evaluate is reported as not checked — never as passed.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from lxml import etree

from .model import Brex, Rule, _first, _local, dmc_of


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ XPath 2.0 functions for lxml
def _s(v) -> str:
    if isinstance(v, list):
        v = v[0] if v else ""
    if isinstance(v, etree._Element):
        return "".join(v.itertext())
    return "" if v is None else str(v)


def _seq(v) -> list[str]:
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return [_s(x) for x in v]
    return [] if v is None else [_s(v)]


def _flags(f) -> int:
    f = _s(f)
    return (re.I if "i" in f else 0) | (re.S if "s" in f else 0) | (re.M if "m" in f else 0) | (re.X if "x" in f else 0)


def _class_end(p: str, i: int) -> tuple[str, str | None, int]:
    """p[i] == '['. -> (positive class body, subtracted class or None, index after the closing ']')."""
    j = i + 1
    body = ""
    if j < len(p) and p[j] == "^":
        body, j = "^", j + 1
    if j < len(p) and p[j] == "]":                     # a ']' right at the start is literal
        body, j = body + "\\]", j + 1
    while j < len(p):
        c = p[j]
        if c == "\\" and j + 1 < len(p):
            body += p[j:j + 2]
            j += 2
            continue
        if c == "-" and j + 1 < len(p) and p[j + 1] == "[":      # XML Schema class subtraction
            sub, j = _xsd_to_py_class(p, j + 1)
            if j < len(p) and p[j] == "]":
                j += 1
            return body, sub, j
        if c == "]":
            return body, None, j + 1
        body += c
        j += 1
    return body, None, j


def _xsd_to_py_class(p: str, i: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    body, sub, j = _class_end(p, i)
    cls = f"[{body}]"
    return (f"(?:(?!{sub}){cls})" if sub else cls), j


def _rx(p: str) -> str:
    """An XML Schema / XPath regular expression in Python's syntax: class subtraction
    ([A-Z-[O]] = A to Z except O) and the XML name escapes \\i and \\c."""
    p = p.replace(r"\i", r"[A-Za-z_:]").replace(r"\c", r"[-\w.:]")
    if "-[" not in p:
        return p
    out, i = "", 0
    while i < len(p):
        c = p[i]
        if c == "\\" and i + 1 < len(p):
            out += p[i:i + 2]
            i += 2
        elif c == "[":
            cls, i = _xsd_to_py_class(p, i)
            out += cls
        else:
            out += c
            i += 1
    return out


XPATH2 = {
    "matches": lambda ctx, s, p, f="": re.search(_rx(_s(p)), _s(s), _flags(f)) is not None,
    "tokenize": lambda ctx, s, p, f="": [t for t in re.split(_rx(_s(p)), _s(s), flags=_flags(f))],
    "replace": lambda ctx, s, p, r, f="": re.sub(_rx(_s(p)), re.sub(r"\$(\d)", r"\\\1", _s(r)), _s(s), flags=_flags(f)),
    "lower-case": lambda ctx, s: _s(s).lower(),
    "upper-case": lambda ctx, s: _s(s).upper(),
    "ends-with": lambda ctx, s, t: _s(s).endswith(_s(t)),
    "string-join": lambda ctx, seq, sep="": _s(sep).join(_seq(seq)),
    "distinct-values": lambda ctx, seq: list(dict.fromkeys(_seq(seq))),
    "compare": lambda ctx, a, b: float((_s(a) > _s(b)) - (_s(a) < _s(b))),
    "exists": lambda ctx, seq: bool(seq) if isinstance(seq, list) else seq is not None,
    "empty": lambda ctx, seq: (not seq) if isinstance(seq, list) else seq is None,
    "abs": lambda ctx, n: abs(float(_s(n) or 0)),
}
_EXT = {(None, k): v for k, v in XPATH2.items()}
# prefixes BREX paths use without declaring them (S1000D conventions)
NS = {"xlink": "http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink", "xsi": "http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance",
      "rdf": "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#", "dc": "http://www.purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"}


@dataclass
class Compiled:
    rule: Rule
    lx: object = None             # lxml XPath, or None
    ep: object = None             # elementpath selector, or None
    error: str | None = None


def compile_rule(rule: Rule) -> Compiled:
    c = Compiled(rule)
    try:
        c.lx = etree.XPath(rule.path, extensions=_EXT, namespaces=NS)
    except etree.XPathSyntaxError:
        c.lx = None
    if c.lx is None:
        c.ep = _ep(rule.path)
        if c.ep is None:
            c.error = "the rule's path is not valid XPath"
    return c


def _ep(path: str):
    try:
        import elementpath
        from elementpath import XPath2Parser
        return elementpath.Selector(path, parser=XPath2Parser, namespaces=NS)
    except Exception:              # noqa: BLE001 - an unusable path is reported, not raised
        return None


def _evaluate(c: Compiled, root):
    if c.lx is not None:
        try:
            return c.lx(root)
        except (etree.XPathEvalError, etree.XPathResultError, TypeError, ValueError, re.error):
            if c.ep is None:
                c.ep = _ep(c.rule.path)
    if c.ep is not None:
        return c.ep.select(root)
    raise ValueError(c.error or "cannot evaluate")


def _items(res) -> list:
    """Normalise an XPath result: the things found (empty list = nothing / false)."""
    if isinstance(res, list):
        return [x for x in res if x is not None]
    if isinstance(res, bool):
        return [True] if res else []
    if isinstance(res, (int, float)):
        return [res] if res else []
    if isinstance(res, str):
        return [res] if res else []
    return [res] if res is not None else []


def _value(x) -> str:
    if isinstance(x, etree._Element):
        return "".join(x.itertext()).strip()
    if hasattr(x, "value") and not isinstance(x, str):        # elementpath attribute node
        return str(x.value)
    return str(x)


def _node_line(x, root) -> tuple[int | None, object]:
    """(line, element) of a found item: elements, attributes and text results map to their element."""
    if isinstance(x, etree._Element):
        return x.sourceline, x
    gp = getattr(x, "getparent", None)
    if callable(gp):
        el = gp()
        if isinstance(el, etree._Element):
            return el.sourceline, el
    el = getattr(x, "parent", None) or getattr(x, "elem", None)
    if isinstance(el, etree._Element):
        return el.sourceline, el
    return None, None


def _value_ok(v: str, values) -> bool:
    for form, allowed, _ in values:
        if form == "single" and v == allowed:
            return True
        if form == "range" and "~" in allowed:
            lo, hi = (x.strip() for x in allowed.split("~", 1))
            try:
                if float(lo) <= float(v) <= float(hi):
                    return True
            except ValueError:
                if lo <= v <= hi:
                    return True
        if form == "pattern":
            try:
                if re.fullmatch(_rx(allowed), v):
                    return True
            except re.error:
                pass
    return False


@dataclass
class Finding:
    rule: Rule
    brex: Brex
    line: int | None
    element: object
    detail: str = ""


@dataclass
class Result:
    findings: list[Finding] = field(default_factory=list)
    checked: int = 0
    not_checked: list[tuple[Rule, str]] = field(default_factory=list)


class CompiledBrex:
    def __init__(self, brex: Brex):
        self.brex = brex
        self.rules = [compile_rule(r) for r in brex.rules]

    def check(self, root, dm_type: str | None, result: Result | None = None) -> Result:
        res = result or Result()
        for c in self.rules:
            r = c.rule
            if r.context and dm_type and r.context != dm_type:
                continue
            try:
                found = _items(_evaluate(c, root))
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - not checked, reported
                res.not_checked.append((r, str(e)[:160]))
                continue
            res.checked += 1
            if r.flag == "1":
                if not found:
                    res.findings.append(Finding(r, self.brex, None, None, "required, but not found"))
                continue
            if r.flag == "2":
                if not r.values:
                    continue
                for x in found:
                    v = _value(x)
                    if not _value_ok(v, r.values):
                        line, el = _node_line(x, root)
                        allowed = ", ".join(f"'{a}'" for _, a, _ in r.values[:8])
                        res.findings.append(Finding(r, self.brex, line, el, f"value '{v}'; allowed: {allowed}"))
                continue
            # flag 0 (and anything unknown): prohibited
            for x in found:
                if r.values and not _value_ok(_value(x), r.values):
                    continue                                       # only the listed values are prohibited
                line, el = _node_line(x, root)
                res.findings.append(Finding(r, self.brex, line, el,
                                            f"value '{_value(x)}'" if r.values else ""))
        self._check_sns(root, res)
        return res

    def _check_sns(self, root, res: Result) -> None:
        sns = self.brex.sns
        if not sns:
            return
        ident = _first(root, "dmIdent")
        code = _first(ident, "dmCode") if ident is not None else None
        if code is None:
            return
        levels = [("system", code.get("systemCode", "")), ("subsystem", code.get("subSystemCode", "")),
                  ("sub-subsystem", code.get("subSubSystemCode", "")), ("assembly", code.get("assyCode", ""))]
        node_children, path = sns, []
        for name, val in levels:
            if not node_children or not val:
                break                                          # an absent code is a schema error, reported there
            if val not in node_children:
                rule = Rule(0, "BREX-SNS", None, "dmCode", "2",
                            f"The {name} code '{val}' of this data module code is not defined in the BREX's SNS "
                            f"({'-'.join(path) or 'top level'}: allowed {', '.join(sorted(node_children)[:12])}"
                            f"{' …' if len(node_children) > 12 else ''}).")
                res.findings.append(Finding(rule, self.brex, code.sourceline, code))
                return
            path.append(val)
            node_children = node_children[val].children
        res.checked += 1


def document_brex_ref(root) -> str | None:
    """The DMC the document names in its brexDmRef (S1000D dmStatus/brexDmRef)."""
    status = _first(root, "dmStatus")
    if status is None:
        status = _first(root, "pmStatus")
    ref = _first(status, "brexDmRef") if status is not None else None
    code = _first(ref, "dmCode") if ref is not None else None
    return dmc_of(code) if code is not None else None

"""Installed BREX data modules: stored in the data folder, found by DMC, chained, compiled once."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import threading
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from .engine import CompiledBrex
from .model import Brex, parse_brex




def _issue_key(issue: str) -> tuple:
    return tuple(int(x) if x.isdigit() else 0 for x in re.split(r"[-.]", issue or "0"))


class BrexLibrary:
    def __init__(self, root: Path):
        self.root = Path(root)
        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.index_file = self.root / "index.json"
        self.alias_file = self.root / "substitutes.json"
        self._compiled: dict[str, tuple[float, CompiledBrex]] = {}
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- index
    def list(self) -> list[dict]:
        if not self.index_file.exists():
            return []
        try:
            return json.loads(self.index_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            return []

    def _save(self, entries: list[dict]) -> None:
        self.index_file.write_text(json.dumps(entries, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    def install(self, data: bytes, source_name: str = "") -> dict:
        """Add (or replace the same DMC and issue of) a BREX data module. Raises ValueError."""
        b = parse_brex(data)
        safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", f"{b.dmc}_{b.issue}") + ".xml"
        with self._lock:
            (self.root / safe).write_bytes(data)
            entries = [e for e in self.list() if not (e["dmc"] == b.dmc and e["issue"] == b.issue)]
            entry = {"dmc": b.dmc, "issue": b.issue, "title": b.title, "schema_issue": b.schema_issue,
                     "parent_dmc": b.parent_dmc, "rules": len(b.rules), "sns_systems": len(b.sns),
                     "file": safe, "source_name": source_name,
                     "installed_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
            entries.append(entry)
            self._save(sorted(entries, key=lambda e: (e["dmc"], _issue_key(e["issue"]))))
            self._compiled.pop(safe, None)
        return entry

    def remove(self, dmc: str, issue: str) -> bool:
        with self._lock:
            entries = self.list()
            keep = [e for e in entries if not (e["dmc"] == dmc and e["issue"] == issue)]
            for e in entries:
                if e not in keep:
                    (self.root / e["file"]).unlink(missing_ok=True)
                    self._compiled.pop(e["file"], None)
            self._save(keep)
            return len(keep) != len(entries)

    def find(self, dmc: str) -> dict | None:
        """The installed BREX with this DMC (the highest issue if several are installed)."""
        hits = [e for e in self.list() if e["dmc"].upper() == dmc.upper()]
        return max(hits, key=lambda e: _issue_key(e["issue"])) if hits else None

    def default_for(self, s1000d_issue: str) -> dict | None:
        """The S1000D default BREX for an issue (modelIdentCode S1000D, written for that issue)."""
        hits = [e for e in self.list() if e["dmc"].upper().startswith("S1000D-") and e.get("schema_issue") == s1000d_issue]
        return max(hits, key=lambda e: _issue_key(e["issue"])) if hits else None

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- substitutes
    def substitutes(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """named DMC -> installed DMC used in its place (chosen by the user)."""
        if not self.alias_file.exists():
            return {}
        try:
            return json.loads(self.alias_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            return {}

    def set_substitute(self, named: str, use: str) -> None:
        if self.find(use) is None:
            raise ValueError(f"DMC-{use} is not installed")
        if named.upper() == use.upper():
            raise ValueError("a BREX cannot stand in for itself")
        with self._lock:
            subs = self.substitutes()
            subs[named] = use
            self.alias_file.write_text(json.dumps(subs, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    def remove_substitute(self, named: str) -> bool:
        with self._lock:
            subs = self.substitutes()
            hit = subs.pop(named, None) is not None
            self.alias_file.write_text(json.dumps(subs, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
            return hit

    def chain(self, dmc: str) -> tuple[list[dict], str | None]:
        """The BREX named by a document and those it builds on. -> (installed chain, first missing DMC).
        A missing BREX with a substitute is replaced by it; such entries carry "substitute_for"."""
        out, seen, cur = [], set(), dmc
        subs = {k.upper(): v for k, v in self.substitutes().items()}
        while cur and cur.upper() not in seen:
            seen.add(cur.upper())
            e = self.find(cur)
            if e is None and cur.upper() in subs:
                e = self.find(subs[cur.upper()])
                if e is not None:
                    e = {**e, "substitute_for": cur}
                    seen.add(e["dmc"].upper())
            if e is None:
                return out, cur
            out.append(e)
            cur = e.get("parent_dmc")
        return out, None

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- compiled rules
    def load(self, entry: dict) -> Brex:
        return self.compiled(entry).brex

    def compiled(self, entry: dict) -> CompiledBrex:
        p = self.root / entry["file"]
        mtime = p.stat().st_mtime
        with self._lock:
            hit = self._compiled.get(entry["file"])
            if hit and hit[0] == mtime:
                return hit[1]
        cb = CompiledBrex(parse_brex(p.read_bytes()))
        with self._lock:
            self._compiled[entry["file"]] = (mtime, cb)
        return cb

"""Reading a BREX data module: identity, the BREX it builds on, and its rules."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from lxml import etree

XSI = "{http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance}"


def _local(el) -> str:
    return etree.QName(el).localname if isinstance(el.tag, str) else ""


def _text(el) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", "".join(el.itertext())).strip() if el is not None else ""


def _first(el, name):
    for d in el.iter():
        if _local(d) == name:
            return d
    return None


def dmc_of(code) -> str:
    """DMC string from a dmCode element: MIC-SDC-SYS-SUBSUBSUB-ASSY-DISDISV-INFOINFOV-ILC."""
    g = lambda k: code.get(k, "")
    return (f"{g('modelIdentCode')}-{g('systemDiffCode')}-{g('systemCode')}-{g('subSystemCode')}{g('subSubSystemCode')}-"
            f"{g('assyCode')}-{g('disassyCode')}{g('disassyCodeVariant')}-{g('infoCode')}{g('infoCodeVariant')}-{g('itemLocationCode')}")


def schema_issue(schema_location: str | None) -> str | None:
    """'4.1' from .../S1000D_4-1/xml_schema_flat/brex.xsd, '6' from .../S1000D_6/..."""
    m = re.search(r"S1000D_(\d+)(?:-(\d+))?", schema_location or "")
    return (m.group(1) + (f".{m.group(2)}" if m.group(2) else "")) if m else None


@dataclass
class Rule:
    index: int
    rule_id: str                  # e.g. BREX-CMMST-00013, or Req_dmRef_01_@caveat_01_A, or #12
    context: str | None           # schema file name the rule is limited to (e.g. "proced.xsd"), None = all
    path: str
    flag: str                     # "0" prohibited | "1" required | "2" allowed (values)
    use: str
    values: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)   # (form, allowed, meaning)


@dataclass
class SnsNode:
    code: str
    title: str
    children: dict[str, "SnsNode"] = field(default_factory=dict)


@dataclass
class Brex:
    dmc: str
    issue: str
    title: str
    schema_issue: str | None
    parent_dmc: str | None        # the BREX this one builds on (None when it refers to itself or to nothing)
    rules: list[Rule]
    sns: dict[str, SnsNode]       # system code -> node (empty: no SNS rules)
    notations: dict[str, bool]    # notation name -> allowed
    text_rules: list[str]         # rules that are prose only (nonContextRules)

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.dmc} issue {self.issue}"


def _rule_id(use: str, index: int) -> str:
    m = re.match(r"\s*(BREX-[A-Z0-9]+-\d+(?:/BREX-[A-Z0-9]+-\d+)*)", use)
    if m:
        return m.group(1)
    m = re.search(r"\[[^\]]*?\b(Req_[^\],\s]+)\]", use)
    if m:
        return m.group(1)
    m = re.match(r"\s*([A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:[-_.][A-Z0-9]+)+)\s*(\([^)]*\))?\s*:", use)   # "SLS-002: ..." project style
    if m:
        return m.group(1)
    return f"rule {index}"


def _sns_tree(parent_el, level_names: list[str]) -> dict[str, SnsNode]:
    if not level_names:
        return {}
    name, rest = level_names[0], level_names[1:]
    out: dict[str, SnsNode] = {}
    for el in parent_el:
        if _local(el) != name:
            continue
        code = _text(next((c for c in el if _local(c) == "snsCode"), None))
        title = _text(next((c for c in el if _local(c) == "snsTitle"), None))
        out[code] = SnsNode(code, title, _sns_tree(el, rest))
    return out


def parse_brex(data: bytes) -> Brex:
    """Raises ValueError if the file is not a BREX data module."""
    p = etree.XMLParser(resolve_entities=False, no_network=True, load_dtd=False, huge_tree=True)
    from ..identify.service import fix_declared_encoding
    try:
        root = etree.fromstring(fix_declared_encoding(data), p)
    except etree.XMLSyntaxError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"not well-formed XML: {e}") from None
    content = _first(root, "content")
    brex_el = next((c for c in content if _local(c) == "brex"), None) if content is not None else None
    if _local(root) != "dmodule" or brex_el is None:
        raise ValueError("this is not a BREX data module (no <content><brex>)")
    code = _first(_first(root, "dmIdent"), "dmCode")
    dmc = dmc_of(code)
    iss = _first(root, "issueInfo")
    issue = f"{iss.get('issueNumber', '')}-{iss.get('inWork', '')}" if iss is not None else ""
    title = " - ".join(x for x in (_text(_first(root, "techName")), _text(_first(root, "infoName"))) if x)
    parent = None
    status = _first(root, "dmStatus")
    ref = _first(status if status is not None else root, "brexDmRef")
    if ref is not None and _first(ref, "dmCode") is not None:
        parent = dmc_of(_first(ref, "dmCode"))
        if parent == dmc:
            parent = None
    rules: list[Rule] = []
    for ctx in (x for x in brex_el.iter() if _local(x) == "contextRules"):
        context = (ctx.get("rulesContext") or "").replace("\\", "/").split("/")[-1] or None
        for r in (x for x in ctx.iter() if _local(x) == "structureObjectRule"):
            op = next((c for c in r if _local(c) == "objectPath"), None)
            if op is None or not (op.text or "").strip():
                continue
            use = _text(next((c for c in r if _local(c) == "objectUse"), None))
            vals = [(v.get("valueForm") or "single", v.get("valueAllowed") or "", _text(v))
                    for v in r.iter() if _local(v) == "objectValue"]
            i = len(rules) + 1
            rules.append(Rule(i, _rule_id(use, i), context, op.text.strip(), op.get("allowedObjectFlag", "0"), use, vals))
    sns_el = _first(brex_el, "snsRules")
    sns = {}
    if sns_el is not None:
        descr = _first(sns_el, "snsDescr")
        sns = _sns_tree(descr if descr is not None else sns_el, ["snsSystem", "snsSubSystem", "snsSubSubSystem", "snsAssy"])
    notations = {n.get("notationName", ""): n.get("allowedNotationFlag", "1") != "0"
                 for n in brex_el.iter() if _local(n) == "notationRule" and n.get("notationName")}
    text_rules = [_text(x) for x in brex_el.iter() if _local(x) == "nonContextRule" and _text(x)]
    return Brex(dmc, issue, title, schema_issue(root.get(f"{XSI}noNamespaceSchemaLocation")), parent, rules, sns,
                notations, text_rules)
