"""Stable IPL item numbers across issues, modifications and variants.

A parts catalogue keeps an item's number for its whole life: a new issue or a variant must not renumber
every item after an added or removed part (that would change every procedure step that cites them, and
every reader's references). Given the baseline IPL, ``stabilize`` keeps each continuing part's item number,
gives new parts a free number between their neighbours (225 between 220 and 230; if no whole number is
free, a letter: 220B), never reuses a number a removed part retired, and lists the retired numbers.

Alternates keep the ATA convention: their main item's number plus a letter (30A).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections import defaultdict


def _key(pn: str | None) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]", "", (pn or "").upper().lstrip("."))


def _num(item: str | None) -> int | None:
    return int(item) if item and re.fullmatch(r"\d+", item) else None


def stabilize(ipl: dict, base: dict | None) -> dict:
    """Re-number ``ipl`` rows in place from ``base``. -> stats."""
    if not base or not base.get("rows"):
        return {"kept": 0, "new": [], "retired": []}
    rows = sorted(ipl["rows"], key=lambda r: r.get("order", 0))
    by_id = {r["id"]: r for r in rows}
    bparent = {r["id"]: r for r in base["rows"]}
    pool: dict[tuple, list] = defaultdict(list)          # (pn, parent pn) -> base items in order
    pool_pn: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
    for b in sorted(base["rows"], key=lambda r: r.get("order", 0)):
        if not b.get("item") or b.get("depth") == 0:
            continue
        ppn = _key((bparent.get(b.get("parent_row")) or {}).get("part_number"))
        pool[(_key(b["part_number"]), ppn)].append(b["item"])
        pool_pn[_key(b["part_number"])].append(b["item"])
    used: set[str] = set()

    def take(lst: list) -> str | None:
        while lst:
            it = lst.pop(0)
            if it not in used:
                return it
        return None

    # 1. continuing parts keep their numbers (same part under the same parent first, then same part anywhere)
    for r in rows:
        if r.get("depth") == 0:
            continue
        ppn = _key((by_id.get(r.get("parent_row")) or {}).get("part_number"))
        it = take(pool[(_key(r["part_number"]), ppn)]) or take(pool_pn[_key(r["part_number"])])
        r["_kept"] = it
        if it:
            used.add(it)
    # a new part that takes the place of a removed part with the same name and role goes next to it
    def norm(x):
        return re.sub(r"[^A-Z]", "", (x or "").upper())
    retired_base = [b for b in base["rows"] if b.get("item") and b.get("depth") != 0 and b["item"] not in used
                    and not b.get("alternate_of") and _num(b["item"])]
    anchors: dict[str, int] = {}
    for r in rows:
        if r.get("depth") != 0 and not r["_kept"] and not r.get("alternate_of"):
            hit = next((b for b in retired_base if norm(b.get("nomenclature")) == norm(r.get("nomenclature"))
                        and b.get("role") == r.get("role")), None)
            if hit:
                anchors[r["id"]] = _num(hit["item"])
                retired_base.remove(hit)
    base_nums = sorted(_num(b["item"]) for b in base["rows"] if _num(b.get("item")))
    base_nums_set = set(base_nums)
    # 2. new main items: a free number between the neighbours that kept theirs
    mains = [r for r in rows if r.get("depth") != 0 and not r.get("alternate_of")]
    new = []
    for i, r in enumerate(mains):
        if r["_kept"] and not re.search(r"[A-Z]$", r["_kept"]):
            r["item"] = r["_kept"]
            continue
        if r["id"] in anchors:                  # replaces a removed part: right after its number
            prev = anchors[r["id"]]
            nxt = next((n for n in base_nums if n > prev), None)
        else:
            prev = next((_num(m["item"]) for m in reversed(mains[:i]) if _num(m.get("item"))), 0)
            nxt = next((_num(m["_kept"]) for m in mains[i + 1:] if _num(m.get("_kept"))), None)
        hi = nxt if nxt is not None else prev + 20
        cand = [n for n in range(prev + 1, hi) if str(n) not in used and n not in base_nums_set]   # never reuse a retired number
        nice = [n for n in cand if n % 5 == 0] or cand
        if nice:
            pick = str(min(nice, key=lambda n: abs(n - (prev + hi) / 2)))
        else:
            base_items = {b.get("item") for b in base["rows"]}
            pick = next(f"{prev}{c}" for c in "BCDEFGHJKLMNPRSTUVWXYZ" if f"{prev}{c}" not in used and f"{prev}{c}" not in base_items)
        r["item"] = pick
        used.add(pick)
        new.append({"row": r["id"], "item": pick, "part_number": r["part_number"],
                    **({"replaces_item": str(anchors[r["id"]])} if r["id"] in anchors else {})})
    # 3. alternates: main item number + letter
    letters = defaultdict(set)
    for r in rows:
        if r.get("alternate_of") and r["_kept"] and re.search(r"[A-Z]$", r["_kept"]):
            main = by_id.get(r["alternate_of"])
            if main and r["_kept"].rstrip("ABCDEFGHJKLMNPRSTUVWXYZ") == main.get("item"):
                r["item"] = r["_kept"]
                letters[r["alternate_of"]].add(r["_kept"][-1])
                continue
        if r.get("alternate_of"):
            r["_pending"] = True
    for r in rows:
        if r.pop("_pending", False):
            main = by_id.get(r["alternate_of"]) or {}
            c = next(c for c in "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPRSTUVWXYZ" if c not in letters[r["alternate_of"]])
            letters[r["alternate_of"]].add(c)
            r["item"] = f"{main.get('item', '?')}{c}"
            if not r["_kept"]:
                new.append({"row": r["id"], "item": r["item"], "part_number": r["part_number"]})
    for r in rows:
        r.pop("_kept", None)
    current = {r["item"] for r in rows}
    retired = sorted({b["item"] for b in base["rows"] if b.get("item") and b.get("depth") != 0} - current,
                     key=lambda x: (_num(re.sub(r"\D", "", x)) or 0, x))
    stats = {"kept": sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("depth") != 0) - len(new), "new": new, "retired": retired}
    ipl["item_numbers"] = stats
    return stats



================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\engineering\parts_import.py
================================================================================

"""Reading a parts list (MBOM / APL / EBOM) from Excel, CSV or PDF, with the ambiguity made visible.

``inspect(path)`` finds every table that could be the parts list (each sheet; each table on each PDF page),
its header row, and a proposed column -> field mapping with how sure it is:

* ``exact``    the header is a known name for the field ("Part Number", "Désignation EN", "Qty.")
* ``guessed``  the header resembles a known name, or the column's values look like the field (part numbers,
               small whole numbers, "*"/"**" levels)
* ``missing``  nothing found

Required fields are part number, description and quantity. When one of them is guessed or missing, or two
tables score alike, the import is marked ``needs_review`` and the writer confirms it on Match 3D to parts list
-> Parts list import. The confirmed mapping is kept per product and per file layout, so the next issue of the
same export loads without asking.

``load(path, mapping)`` reads the records with a confirmed (or proposed) mapping, in the format the
reconciler expects.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import difflib
import hashlib
import re
from pathlib import Path

from ..reconcile.column_mapping import DEFAULT_COLUMN_MAP, normalize_header_text
from ..reconcile.mbom_loader import _clean_cell

FIELDS = {
    "part_number": "Part number", "description": "Description", "qty": "Quantity", "level": "Level / indenture",
    "manuf_code": "CAGE / manufacturer", "unit_measure": "Unit", "find_number": "Find / item number",
    "seq_number": "Sequence number", "equiv": "Equivalence (J/K alternates)", "amdt": "Amendment",
    "comments": "Remarks", "material_spec": "Material", "class": "Class", "status": "Status",
    "cad_reference": "3D / CAD reference", "authority": "Authority",
}
REQUIRED = ("part_number", "description", "qty")
KEYWORDS = {                                     # words that suggest a field when no known header matches
    "part_number": ["part", "pn", "p/n", "réf", "reference", "ref", "pnr", "partno", "numéro", "numero", "pièce"],
    "description": ["desc", "nomen", "désign", "design", "name", "libell", "title"],
    "qty": ["qty", "qté", "quant", "upa", "nbr", "nb", "count", "nombre"],
    "level": ["lev", "niv", "indent", "depth"],
    "manuf_code": ["cage", "mfr", "manuf", "fabric", "vendor", "supplier", "fournisseur"],
    "unit_measure": ["uom", "unit", "unité"],
    "find_number": ["find", "item", "pos", "repère", "repere"],
    "seq_number": ["seq"],
    "comments": ["remark", "comment", "note", "obs"],
}


def _header_score(text: str) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    """-> ({field: 'exact'|'guessed'}, {field: score}) for one header cell."""
    norm = normalize_header_text(text)
    if not norm:
        return {}, {}
    hit, score = {}, {}
    for f, variants in DEFAULT_COLUMN_MAP.items():
        vs = {normalize_header_text(v) for v in variants}
        if norm in vs:
            hit[f], score[f] = "exact", 1.0
            continue
        r = max(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, norm, v).ratio() for v in vs)
        kw = any(k.replace(" ", "") in norm for k in KEYWORDS.get(f, []))
        s = max(r, 0.72 if kw else 0)
        if s >= 0.72:
            hit[f], score[f] = "guessed", round(s, 2)
    return hit, score


_PN = re.compile(r"^\.*[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9\-./]{3,}$", re.I)


def _value_score(values: list[str]) -> dict:
    """What the values of a column look like (used when headers are unknown or ambiguous)."""
    vals = [v for v in values if v][:60]
    if len(vals) < 3:
        return {}
    n = len(vals)
    pn = sum(1 for v in vals if _PN.match(v) and re.search(r"\d", v)) / n
    num = sum(1 for v in vals if re.fullmatch(r"\d+([.,]\d+)?", v)) / n
    small_int = sum(1 for v in vals if re.fullmatch(r"\d{1,3}([.,]0+)?", v)) / n
    stars = sum(1 for v in vals if re.fullmatch(r"\*+|\d", v)) / n
    words = sum(1 for v in vals if len(v.split()) >= 2 and re.search(r"[A-Za-z]{3}", v)) / n
    cage = sum(1 for v in vals if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z0-9]{5}", v, re.I) and re.search(r"\d", v)) / n
    distinct = len(set(vals)) / n
    out = {}
    if pn > 0.7 and distinct > 0.5:
        out["part_number"] = pn
    if words > 0.6:
        out["description"] = words
    ints = [int(float(v.replace(",", "."))) for v in vals if re.fullmatch(r"\d+([.,]0+)?", v)]
    rising = len(ints) >= 3 and all(b > a for a, b in zip(ints, ints[1:]))
    if rising and distinct > 0.95:                  # 10, 20, 30…: item / find numbers, not quantities
        out["find_number"] = 0.85
    elif small_int > 0.8 and num > 0.8:
        out["qty"] = small_int * 0.9
    if stars > 0.9 and distinct < 0.3:
        out["level"] = stars
    if cage > 0.8 and distinct < 0.5:
        out["manuf_code"] = cage
    return out


def _tables(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    """Every candidate table: {id, label, rows}."""
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    out = []
    if suffix == ".csv":
        import pandas as pd
        out.append({"id": "csv", "label": path.name, "rows": pd.read_csv(path, header=None, dtype=str).values.tolist()})
    elif suffix in (".xlsx", ".xls", ".xlsm"):
        import pandas as pd
        for name, df in pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name=None, header=None, dtype=str).items():
            out.append({"id": f"sheet:{name}", "label": f"Sheet “{name}”", "rows": df.values.tolist()})
    elif suffix == ".pdf":
        import pdfplumber
        with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:
            for pno, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1):
                for ti, t in enumerate(page.extract_tables() or [], start=1):
                    out.append({"id": f"pdf:{pno}:{ti}", "label": f"Page {pno}, table {ti}", "rows": t, "page": pno})
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"a parts list is .xlsx, .xls, .csv or .pdf (got {suffix})")
    for t in out:
        t["rows"] = [[_clean_cell(c) for c in r] for r in t["rows"]]
    return out


def _propose(rows: list[list[str]]) -> dict | None:
    """Best header row in the first 25 rows, and its mapping. Each (field, column) pair is scored from the
    header text and from what the values below look like; columns are then assigned greedily, one field per
    column and one column per field, so a header that only sounds right cannot beat a column whose values are
    clearly part numbers."""
    best = None
    for i, row in enumerate(rows[:25]):
        if sum(1 for c in row if c) < 2:
            continue
        body = rows[i + 1:i + 61]
        width = max([len(row)] + [len(r) for r in body])
        cand = []                                   # (score, field, column, how, why)
        for ci in range(width):
            head = row[ci] if ci < len(row) else ""
            hit, sc = _header_score(head)
            vals = _value_score([r[ci] if ci < len(r) else "" for r in body])
            for f in set(hit) | set(vals):
                h, v = sc.get(f, 0.0), vals.get(f, 0.0)
                if hit.get(f) == "exact":
                    cand.append((2.0 + v, f, ci, "exact", None))
                    continue
                score = h + 0.9 * v
                if f in ("part_number", "description", "qty") and h and not v and body:
                    score -= 0.4                    # the header sounds right but the values do not fit
                if score >= 0.7:
                    why = "header and values" if h and v else "values look like this field" if v else None
                    cand.append((score, f, ci, "guessed", why))
        mapping, used, total = {}, set(), 0.0
        for score, f, ci, how, why in sorted(cand, key=lambda c: -c[0]):
            if f in mapping or ci in used:
                continue
            mapping[f] = {"column": ci, "header": row[ci] if ci < len(row) else "", "how": how, **({"why": why} if why else {})}
            used.add(ci)
            total += score
        exact = sum(1 for m in mapping.values() if m["how"] == "exact")
        score = exact * 2 + len(mapping) + total * 0.2 + (3 if "part_number" in mapping else -10)
        if best is None or score > best["score"]:
            best = {"header_row": i, "mapping": mapping, "score": round(score, 2)}
    return best


def signature(headers: list[str]) -> str:
    """Identifies a file layout (the header texts), so a confirmed mapping is reused for the next issue."""
    return hashlib.sha1("|".join(normalize_header_text(h) for h in headers).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]


def inspect(path: str | Path) -> dict:
    path = Path(path)
    tables = []
    for t in _tables(path):
        p = _propose(t["rows"])
        if not p or "part_number" not in p["mapping"]:
            continue
        hdr = t["rows"][p["header_row"]]
        body = [r for r in t["rows"][p["header_row"] + 1:] if any(r)]
        pn_col = p["mapping"]["part_number"]["column"]
        data_rows = sum(1 for r in body if pn_col < len(r) and r[pn_col])
        tables.append({"id": t["id"], "label": t["label"], "header_row": p["header_row"], "headers": hdr,
                       "signature": signature(hdr), "mapping": p["mapping"], "score": p["score"], "rows": data_rows,
                       "sample": body[:8], "page": t.get("page")})
    if not tables:
        return {"file": path.name, "tables": [], "chosen": None, "needs_review": True,
                "problems": ["No table with a part-number column was found. A scanned (image) PDF needs OCR first; "
                             "for a spreadsheet, check that the parts list has a header row."]}
    tables.sort(key=lambda t: (-t["score"], -t["rows"]))
    chosen = tables[0]
    pdf = path.suffix.lower() == ".pdf"
    def heads(t):
        return {f: normalize_header_text(m["header"]) for f, m in t["mapping"].items() if m.get("header")}

    def continues(t, c):                            # same part-number header and most mapped headers in common
        a, b = heads(t), heads(c)
        return a.get("part_number") == b.get("part_number") and len(set(a.items()) & set(b.items())) >= min(3, len(b))

    if pdf:                                         # a PDF parts list continues over pages, sometimes re-laid out
        same = [t for t in tables if continues(t, chosen)]
        chosen = {**chosen, "id": "pdf:*", "label": f"{len(same)} table(s) with this layout on pages "
                  + ", ".join(sorted({str(t['page']) for t in same}, key=int)),
                  "rows": sum(t["rows"] for t in same), "parts": [t["id"] for t in same]}
    problems = []
    for f in REQUIRED:
        m = chosen["mapping"].get(f)
        if not m:
            problems.append(f"No column was found for {FIELDS[f].lower()}.")
        elif m["how"] != "exact":
            problems.append(f"{FIELDS[f]} was guessed from “{m['header'] or 'values'}”"
                            + (f" ({m['why']})" if m.get("why") else "") + ".")
    others = [t for t in tables if not (continues(t, chosen) if pdf else t["id"] == chosen["id"])]
    if others and others[0]["score"] >= chosen["score"] - 1:
        problems.append(f"{others[0]['label']} could also be the parts list.")
    if "level" not in chosen["mapping"]:
        problems.append("No level column: the structure is taken from leading dots in the part numbers, if any.")
    return {"file": path.name, "tables": tables, "chosen": chosen, "problems": problems,
            "needs_review": any(not chosen["mapping"].get(f) or chosen["mapping"][f]["how"] != "exact" for f in REQUIRED)
                            or bool(others and others[0]["score"] >= chosen["score"] - 1),
            "layouts": sorted({t["signature"] for t in tables if t["id"] in chosen.get("parts", [chosen["id"]])})}


def load(path: str | Path, mapping: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """mapping = {"table": id | "pdf:*", "signature": ..., "columns": {field: header text}}. Headers are matched by
    text, so the same mapping works on every page of a PDF even when column positions shift."""
    path = Path(path)
    cols = {f: normalize_header_text(h) for f, h in (mapping.get("columns") or {}).items() if h is not None}
    if "part_number" not in cols:
        raise ValueError("the parts list mapping has no part-number column")
    want_table = mapping.get("table")
    records = []
    for t in _tables(path):
        if want_table and want_table != "pdf:*" and t["id"] != want_table:
            continue
        rows = t["rows"]
        hdr_i = None
        for i, row in enumerate(rows[:25]):
            norm = [normalize_header_text(c) for c in row]
            if cols["part_number"] in norm and sum(1 for h in cols.values() if h in norm) >= min(2, len(cols)):
                hdr_i = i
                break
        if hdr_i is None:
            continue
        norm = [normalize_header_text(c) for c in rows[hdr_i]]
        idx = {f: norm.index(h) for f, h in cols.items() if h in norm}
        for row in rows[hdr_i + 1:]:
            rec = {f: (row[i] if i < len(row) else "") for f, i in idx.items()}
            rec = {k: v for k, v in rec.items() if v not in (None, "")}
            if rec.get("part_number") and normalize_header_text(rec["part_number"]) != cols["part_number"]:
                records.append(rec)
        if want_table and want_table != "pdf:*":
            break
    if not records:
        raise ValueError("no parts were read with this mapping")
    return records


def mapping_from_proposal(chosen: dict) -> dict:
    return {"table": chosen["id"], "signature": chosen["signature"],
            "columns": {f: m["header"] for f, m in chosen["mapping"].items() if m.get("header")}}



================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\engineering\roles.py

"""Part roles: what kind of thing a part is, for IPL rules, sequencing and wording.

A role drives three things:

* the IPL (attaching parts are listed after the part they attach; permanent items are
  listed but never removed in disassembly);
* the sequence planner (permanent parts ride with their carrier; seals ride with the
  part they sit on);
* the procedure wording ("Remove and discard the packings", "Do not remove the inserts").

Rules are data (ordered regular expressions over part number and nomenclature, then
geometry). Projects can extend them in ``studio.yaml`` (``roles.extra_rules``) without
code changes. The first matching rule wins; every result records which rule decided it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

ROLES = {
    "fastener":   {"label": "Fastener", "attaching": True,  "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "washer":     {"label": "Washer",   "attaching": True,  "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "nut":        {"label": "Nut",      "attaching": True,  "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "lockwire":   {"label": "Lock wire / safety cable", "attaching": True, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": True},
    "seal":       {"label": "Seal / packing", "attaching": False, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": True},
    "backup_ring": {"label": "Back-up ring", "attaching": False, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": True},
    "insert":     {"label": "Thread insert", "attaching": False, "permanent": True,  "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "press_plug": {"label": "Press-fit plug (Lee plug)", "attaching": False, "permanent": True, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "plate":      {"label": "Bonded plate / label", "attaching": False, "permanent": True, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "fitting":    {"label": "Fitting / union", "attaching": False, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "cap":        {"label": "Protective / storage cap", "attaching": False, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "spring":     {"label": "Spring", "attaching": False, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "bush":       {"label": "Bush / bushing", "attaching": False, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "closure":    {"label": "Threaded plug / cover", "attaching": False, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "moving":     {"label": "Moving part (piston, valve, spool)", "attaching": False, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "housing":    {"label": "Body / housing", "attaching": False, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "lru":        {"label": "Sub-assembly / LRU", "attaching": False, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "marker":     {"label": "Reference marker (no physical part)", "attaching": False, "permanent": True, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "process":    {"label": "Process / material specification", "attaching": False, "permanent": True, "consumable_on_removal": False},
    "part":       {"label": "Part", "attaching": False, "permanent": False, "consumable_on_removal": False},
}

# (role, field, pattern) — field: "pn" (normalised part number) or "name" (nomenclature, upper case)
DEFAULT_RULES: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = [
    ("process", "pn", r"^(NCT|IFC|PCS-|DRSE)"),
    ("marker", "name", r"\b(CENTER|CENTRE) OF GRAVITY\b|\bCDG\b|\bSKELETON\b|\bENVELOPE\b"),
    ("marker", "pn", r"-CDG$"),
    ("lockwire", "name", r"\bLOCK ?WIRE\b|\bSAFETY (CABLE|WIRE)\b|\bFIL FREIN\b|\bCABLE\b|\bFERRULE\b"),
    ("backup_ring", "name", r"\bBACK[- ]?UP RING\b|\bANTI[- ]?EXTRUSION\b"),
    ("seal", "name", r"\bO[- ]?RING\b|\bPACKING\b|\bSEAL\b|\bJOINT\b|\bGASKET\b"),
    ("seal", "pn", r"^(M83461|M83248|M25988|MS28775|MS29513|NAS1611|NAS1612|AS568)"),
    ("backup_ring", "pn", r"^(M8791|MS28774|MS28782)"),
    ("insert", "name", r"\bINSERT\b|\bHELICOIL\b|\bHELI-?COIL\b|\bKEENSERT\b"),
    ("insert", "pn", r"^(MS21209|NAS1130|MS124\d{3}|2TLF|\d{11}$)"),
    ("press_plug", "name", r"\bLEE PLUG\b|\bEXPANDER\b|\bBETA PLUG\b"),
    ("press_plug", "pn", r"^PLG[A-Z]?\d"),
    ("plate", "name", r"\bPLATE\b.*\b(IDENT|AMEND|NAME|DATA)|\b(IDENT|AMEND|NAME|DATA)\w*\s+PLATE\b|\bLABEL\b|\bPLAQU"),
    ("cap", "name", r"\bPROTECTIVE CAP\b|\bSTORAGE PLUG\b|\bDUST CAP\b|\bBOUCHON\b"),
    ("cap", "pn", r"^(MS21914|MS21913)"),
    ("washer", "name", r"\bWASHER\b|\bRONDELLE\b"),
    ("washer", "pn", r"^(NAS1149|AN960|MS15795|NAS620)"),
    ("nut", "name", r"\bNUT\b|\bECROU\b"),
    ("fastener", "name", r"\bSCREW\b|\bBOLT\b|\bVIS\b|\bSTUD\b|\bRIVET\b"),
    ("fastener", "pn", r"^(NAS13\d\d|NAS6\d\d|MS2\d{4}|AN[34]\d|C77\d{3})"),
    ("fitting", "name", r"\bUNION\b|\bFITTING\b|\bADAPTER\b|\bNIPPLE\b|\bROSAN\b|\bRACCORD\b"),
    ("fitting", "pn", r"^AS4099"),
    ("spring", "name", r"\bSPRING\b|\bRESSORT\b"),
    ("closure", "name", r"\bPLUG\b|\bCOVER\b|\bBLANKING\b"),
    ("bush", "name", r"\bBUSH(ING)?\b|\bBAGUE\b|\bSLEEVE\b"),
    ("lru", "name", r"\bSOLENOID\b|\bACTUATOR\b|\bMOTOR\b|\bSENSOR\b|\bTRANSDUCER\b|\bSWITCH\b|\bSERVO"),
    ("moving", "name", r"\bPISTON\b|\bVALVE\b|\bSPOOL\b|\bPOPPET\b|\bPLUNGER\b|\bSLIDE\b"),
    ("housing", "name", r"\bBODY\b|\bHOUSING\b|\bMANIFOLD\b|\bCASE\b|\bCARTER\b|\bCORPS\b"),
]


@dataclass
class RoleDecision:
    role: str
    rule: str
    confidence: float

    def as_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {"role": self.role, "rule": self.rule, "confidence": self.confidence, **ROLES[self.role]}


def normalise_pn(pn: str, manuf_prefix: str | None = None) -> str:
    p = (pn or "").strip().upper().lstrip(".")
    if manuf_prefix and p.startswith(manuf_prefix.upper() + "-"):
        p = p[len(manuf_prefix) + 1:]
    return p


class RoleClassifier:
    def __init__(self, extra_rules: list[tuple[str, str, str]] | None = None):
        rules = list(extra_rules or []) + DEFAULT_RULES
        self.rules = [(role, fld, re.compile(pat, re.I)) for role, fld, pat in rules if role in ROLES]

    def classify(self, part_number: str, names: list[str], geometry: dict | None = None,
                 is_assembly: bool = False, manuf_prefix: str | None = None) -> RoleDecision:
        pn = normalise_pn(part_number, manuf_prefix)
        texts = [n.upper() for n in names if n]
        for role, fld, rx in self.rules:
            if fld == "pn" and rx.search(pn):
                return RoleDecision(role, f"part number /{rx.pattern}/", 0.9)
            if fld == "name" and any(rx.search(t) for t in texts):
                return RoleDecision(role, f"nomenclature /{rx.pattern}/", 0.85)
        if geometry is not None and not geometry.get("bbox"):
            return RoleDecision("marker", "no geometry", 0.7)
        if is_assembly:
            return RoleDecision("lru", "STEP sub-assembly", 0.6)
        if geometry and geometry.get("bbox"):
            b = geometry["bbox"]
            dims = sorted([b[3] - b[0], b[4] - b[1], b[5] - b[2]], reverse=True)
            cyl = geometry.get("cylinders") or []
            if dims[0] / max(dims[2], 1e-6) > 2.5 and cyl and max(c["faces"] for c in cyl) >= 2 and dims[1] < 15:
                return RoleDecision("fastener", "geometry: slender, cylindrical", 0.4)
        return RoleDecision("part", "default", 0.3)

================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\llm\providers.py

"""Pluggable LLM providers. Selected by configuration; ``none`` is the default.

The procedure engine never needs an LLM: templates produce complete STE text. When a
provider is configured it is used only to *improve wording*, and every suggestion must pass
the same STE and fact checks as the template text — otherwise the template text is kept.

Providers:
* ``none``       — templates only (offline, deterministic)
* ``anthropic``  — Anthropic API (``ANTHROPIC_API_KEY``)
* ``bedrock``    — Amazon Bedrock Converse API (AWS credentials; model id configurable,
                   e.g. ``eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0`` as in TechPub)
* ``ollama``     — a local Ollama server (offline): Qwen, Llama, Mistral… through its OpenAI-compatible API
* ``openai``     — any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM, LM Studio, LocalAI, an internal gateway)

Local models: steps are sent in small batches (``batch_size``) so they fit a small context window, and
"thinking" output (``<think>…</think>``, as Qwen 3 and DeepSeek-R1 write) is removed before the JSON is read.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import os
import re
import time

log = logging.getLogger("studio.llm")


class LLMError(Exception):
    pass


class LLMProvider:
    name = "none"

    def available(self) -> bool:
        return False

    def complete(self, system: str, user: str, max_tokens: int = 2000) -> tuple[str, dict]:
        raise LLMError("no LLM provider configured")

    def describe(self) -> dict:
        return {"provider": self.name, "available": self.available()}


class NoneProvider(LLMProvider):
    pass


class AnthropicProvider(LLMProvider):
    name = "anthropic"

    def __init__(self, model: str | None = None, api_key: str | None = None):
        self.model = model or os.environ.get("STUDIO_LLM_MODEL", "claude-sonnet-4-5")
        self.api_key = api_key or os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")

    def available(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.api_key)

    def complete(self, system, user, max_tokens=2000):
        import httpx
        r = httpx.post("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages", timeout=120,
                       headers={"x-api-key": self.api_key, "anthropic-version": "2023-06-01",
                                "content-type": "application/json"},
                       json={"model": self.model, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "system": system,
                             "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": user}]})
        if r.status_code >= 400:
            raise LLMError(f"Anthropic API {r.status_code}: {r.text[:300]}")
        d = r.json()
        text = "".join(b.get("text", "") for b in d.get("content", []))
        u = d.get("usage", {})
        return text, {"input_tokens": u.get("input_tokens", 0), "output_tokens": u.get("output_tokens", 0)}

    def describe(self):
        return {**super().describe(), "model": self.model}


class BedrockProvider(LLMProvider):
    name = "bedrock"

    def __init__(self, model: str | None = None, region: str | None = None, endpoint_url: str | None = None,
                 profile: str | None = None):
        self.model = model or os.environ.get("STUDIO_LLM_MODEL", "eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0")
        self.region = region or os.environ.get("AWS_REGION", "eu-west-3")
        vpce = os.environ.get("BEDROCK_VPCE_DNS")
        self.endpoint_url = endpoint_url or (f"https://{vpce}" if vpce else None)     # VPC interface endpoint
        self.profile = profile or os.environ.get("AWS_PROFILE")

    def _session(self):
        import boto3
        return boto3.Session(profile_name=self.profile, region_name=self.region) if self.profile else boto3.Session(region_name=self.region)

    def available(self) -> bool:
        try:
            return bool(self._session().get_credentials())
        except Exception:
            return False

    def complete(self, system, user, max_tokens=2000):
        c = self._session().client("bedrock-runtime", region_name=self.region,
                                   **({"endpoint_url": self.endpoint_url} if self.endpoint_url else {}))
        r = c.converse(modelId=self.model, system=[{"text": system}],
                       messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": user}]}],
                       inferenceConfig={"maxTokens": max_tokens, "temperature": 0.0})
        text = "".join(p.get("text", "") for p in r["output"]["message"]["content"])
        u = r.get("usage", {})
        return text, {"input_tokens": u.get("inputTokens", 0), "output_tokens": u.get("outputTokens", 0)}

    def describe(self):
        return {**super().describe(), "model": self.model, "region": self.region, "endpoint_url": self.endpoint_url}


class OpenAICompatProvider(LLMProvider):
    name = "openai"

    default_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1"
    default_model = "llama3.1"

    def __init__(self, base_url: str | None = None, model: str | None = None, api_key: str | None = None,
                 json_mode: bool = True, timeout: float = 300):
        self.base_url = (base_url or os.environ.get("STUDIO_LLM_BASE_URL", self.default_url)).rstrip("/")
        self.model = model or os.environ.get("STUDIO_LLM_MODEL", self.default_model)
        self.api_key = api_key or os.environ.get("STUDIO_LLM_API_KEY", "none")
        self.json_mode, self.timeout = json_mode, float(timeout)
        self._ok: tuple[float, bool] | None = None

    def models(self) -> list[str]:
        import httpx
        r = httpx.get(self.base_url + "/models", timeout=5, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.api_key}"})
        r.raise_for_status()
        return sorted(m.get("id") for m in r.json().get("data", []) if m.get("id"))

    def available(self) -> bool:
        if self._ok and time.monotonic() - self._ok[0] < 30:   # the header asks often; ask the server at most every 30 s
            return self._ok[1]
        try:
            import httpx
            ok = httpx.get(self.base_url + "/models", timeout=2,
                           headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.api_key}"}).status_code < 500
        except Exception:
            ok = False
        self._ok = (time.monotonic(), ok)
        return ok

    def complete(self, system, user, max_tokens=2000):
        import httpx
        thinking = re.search(r"qwen3|deepseek-r1|qwq", self.model or "", re.I)
        if thinking and "qwen3" in self.model.lower():
            user = user + "\n/no_think"                  # Qwen 3: answer directly, no thinking pass
        body = {"model": self.model, "temperature": 0,
                "max_tokens": max_tokens * 3 if thinking else max_tokens,   # room left if it thinks anyway
                "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]}
        if self.json_mode:
            body["response_format"] = {"type": "json_object"}
        r = httpx.post(self.base_url + "/chat/completions", timeout=self.timeout,
                       headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.api_key}"}, json=body)
        if r.status_code == 400 and self.json_mode and "response_format" in r.text:
            body.pop("response_format")                  # servers without JSON mode
            r = httpx.post(self.base_url + "/chat/completions", timeout=self.timeout,
                           headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.api_key}"}, json=body)
        if r.status_code >= 400:
            raise LLMError(f"LLM endpoint {r.status_code}: {r.text[:300]}")
        d = r.json()
        u = d.get("usage", {})
        return d["choices"][0]["message"]["content"], {"input_tokens": u.get("prompt_tokens", 0),
                                                       "output_tokens": u.get("completion_tokens", 0)}

    def describe(self):
        return {**super().describe(), "model": self.model, "base_url": self.base_url}


class OllamaProvider(OpenAICompatProvider):
    """Ollama on this machine or the local network (``ollama serve``; ``ollama pull qwen2.5:7b``)."""
    name = "ollama"
    default_url = "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"
    default_model = "qwen2.5:7b"


PROVIDERS = {"none": NoneProvider, "anthropic": AnthropicProvider, "bedrock": BedrockProvider,
             "ollama": OllamaProvider, "openai": OpenAICompatProvider}
SETTING_KEYS = ("model", "region", "base_url", "api_key", "endpoint_url", "profile", "json_mode", "timeout")


def get_provider(cfg: dict | None = None) -> LLMProvider:
    cfg = cfg or {}
    name = (cfg.get("provider") or os.environ.get("STUDIO_LLM_PROVIDER") or "none").lower()
    cls = PROVIDERS.get(name, NoneProvider)
    import inspect
    accepted = set(inspect.signature(cls.__init__).parameters)
    kwargs = {k: v for k, v in cfg.items() if k in SETTING_KEYS and k in accepted and v not in (None, "")}
    if cfg.get("api_key_env") and "api_key" in accepted and not kwargs.get("api_key"):
        kwargs["api_key"] = os.environ.get(cfg["api_key_env"])
    prov = cls(**kwargs)
    prov.batch_size = int(cfg.get("batch_size") or (8 if name == "ollama" else 15))   # small local models: small batches
    return prov


REFINE_SYSTEM = """You edit aircraft maintenance procedure steps written in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
Rules: imperative, one instruction per sentence, max 20 words per sentence, approved STE verbs only,
no modal verbs, active voice. Keep every item number in parentheses, every quantity and every torque
value exactly as given. Do not add facts, tools, parts or values. If a step is already correct, return it unchanged.
Answer with JSON only: {"steps": [{"id": "...", "text": "..."}]}"""


def _json_from(text: str) -> dict:
    """The JSON object in a model's answer, after removing thinking blocks and code fences."""
    text = re.sub(r"<think>.*?</think>", "", text, flags=re.S | re.I)
    text = re.sub(r"```(?:json)?", "", text)
    start, end = text.find("{"), text.rfind("}")
    if start < 0 or end < start:
        raise LLMError("the answer contains no JSON object")
    return json.loads(text[start:end + 1])


def refine_steps(provider: LLMProvider, steps: list[dict], context: str, batch_size: int = 12) -> tuple[dict[str, str], dict]:
    """Ask the provider for improved wording, a batch of steps at a time. Returns ({step_id: text}, usage).
    Never raises: a batch that fails keeps its template text."""
    if not provider.available() or not steps:
        return {}, {}
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    usage = {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "batches": 0, "failed_batches": 0, "seconds": 0.0}
    errors = []
    for i in range(0, len(steps), max(1, batch_size)):
        batch = steps[i:i + batch_size]
        user = context + "\n\nSteps:\n" + json.dumps([{"id": s["id"], "text": s["text"]} for s in batch], indent=1)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            text, u = provider.complete(REFINE_SYSTEM, user)
            data = _json_from(text)
            ids = {s["id"] for s in batch}
            out.update({s["id"]: s["text"] for s in data.get("steps", []) if s.get("id") in ids and s.get("text")})
            usage["input_tokens"] += u.get("input_tokens", 0)
            usage["output_tokens"] += u.get("output_tokens", 0)
        except Exception as e:  # provider down, bad JSON: these steps keep the template text
            usage["failed_batches"] += 1
            errors.append(str(e)[:200])
            log.warning("LLM refinement of a batch skipped: %s", e)
        usage["batches"] += 1
        usage["seconds"] = round(usage["seconds"] + time.monotonic() - t0, 1)
    if errors:
        usage["error"] = errors[0]
    return out, usage


def test_provider(provider: LLMProvider) -> dict:
    """Send two sample steps through the real refinement path; report what came back and how long it took."""
    sample = [{"id": "t1", "text": "Carefully remove the six screws (220) and the six washers (230) from the plugs (210)."},
              {"id": "t2", "text": "Torque the six screws (220) to 10 to 11 N.m (88.5 to 97.4 lbf.in)."}]
    if not provider.available():
        return {"ok": False, "message": f"{provider.name}: not reachable or not configured", **provider.describe()}
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    try:
        text, usage = provider.complete(REFINE_SYSTEM, "Component: hydraulic valve.\n\nSteps:\n" + json.dumps(sample, indent=1))
        data = _json_from(text)
        return {"ok": True, "seconds": round(time.monotonic() - t0, 1), "usage": usage, "sample": sample,
                "answer": data.get("steps", []), **provider.describe()}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"ok": False, "seconds": round(time.monotonic() - t0, 1), "message": str(e)[:400], **provider.describe()}

================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\procedures\generator.py

"""Procedures (assembly / disassembly) from the process graph: text, requirements, checks.

Output is one *neutral procedure model* per kind (``studio.procedure/1``) that every
publisher renders (S1000D, ATA iSpec 2200, the editor JSON). Every step keeps:
``op_ids`` (the operations it words), ``occ_ids`` (3D) and ``rows`` (IPL), the STE / fact
check findings, and where its text came from (``template`` / ``llm`` / ``writer``).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections import defaultdict

from ..llm.providers import LLMProvider, NoneProvider, refine_steps
from .ste import STEChecker, fact_check, technical_names_from
from .text import clean_name, plural, ref, sentences_for, supply_ref
from ..process.graph import wrench_for

SAFETY_RULES = [
    {"id": "wrn-hydraulic", "kind": "warning", "match": ("text", r"SKYDROL|PHOSPHATE ESTER|HYDRAULIC FLUID"),
     "where": "preliminary",
     "text": "HYDRAULIC FLUID (PHOSPHATE ESTER) IS DANGEROUS. WEAR GLOVES AND GOGGLES. IF THE FLUID GETS ON YOUR SKIN "
             "OR IN YOUR EYES, FLUSH IT AWAY WITH WATER AND GET MEDICAL AID."},
    {"id": "wrn-spring", "kind": "warning", "match": ("role", "spring"), "where": "spring",
     "text": "THE SPRING IS COMPRESSED. HOLD THE PARTS AND RELEASE THE SPRING SLOWLY. IF YOU DO NOT, THE PARTS CAN "
             "MOVE SUDDENLY AND CAUSE INJURY."},
    {"id": "cau-packing", "kind": "caution", "match": ("role", "seal"), "where": "seal_removal",
     "text": "DO NOT USE A SHARP TOOL TO REMOVE THE PACKINGS. A SCRATCH ON THE SEAL GROOVE CAN CAUSE A LEAK."},
]


def _safety(ipl: dict) -> list[dict]:
    rows = ipl["rows"]
    out = []
    for rule in SAFETY_RULES:
        kind, pat = rule["match"]
        if kind == "text":
            # MBOM comments and STEP descriptions often say "(POUR SKYDROL)" on the packings
            ev = [r for r in rows if re.search(pat, " ".join(str(r.get(k) or "") for k in
                                                         ("nomenclature_mbom", "mbom_comments", "step_name", "step_description")), re.I)]
            if not ev:
                continue
            evidence = [f"{r['part_number']}: {r.get('step_description') or r.get('mbom_comments') or r.get('nomenclature_mbom')}" for r in ev][:3]
        else:
            ev = [r for r in rows if r["role"] == pat]
            if not ev:
                continue
            evidence = [f"{r['part_number']} ({r['role']})" for r in ev][:3]
        out.append({**rule, "evidence": evidence, "source": f"rule:{rule['id']}"})
    return out


_MINOR = {"fastener", "washer", "nut", "seal", "backup_ring", "lockwire"}


def _title(st: dict, kind: str, ipl: dict, names: dict | None) -> str:
    if st.get("title") and st["id"] in ("st-d00", "st-a98", "st-a99") or "stay installed" in (st.get("title") or ""):
        return st["title"]
    rows = {r["id"]: r for r in ipl["rows"]}
    if st.get("kind") == "attaching" and st.get("rows") and st["rows"][0] in rows:
        a = rows[st["rows"][0]]
        n = clean_name({**a, "count": 1}, names)
        return f"Remove the attaching parts from the {n}" if kind == "disassembly" else f"Install the attaching parts on the {n}"
    if st.get("kind") in ("disassemble", "assemble") and st.get("assy_row") in rows:
        a = rows[st["assy_row"]]
        return f"{'Disassemble' if kind == 'disassembly' else 'Assemble'} the {clean_name({**a, 'count': 1}, names)}"
    mains = [rows[r] for r in st["rows"] if r in rows and rows[r]["role"] not in _MINOR] or \
            [rows[r] for r in st["rows"][:1] if r in rows]
    parts = []
    for r in mains:
        n = clean_name({**r, "count": r.get("units_per_assy")}, names)
        n = plural(n) if (r.get("units_per_assy") or 1) > 1 else n
        if f"the {n}" not in parts:
            parts.append(f"the {n}")
    verb = "Remove" if kind == "disassembly" else "Install"
    if not mains and st.get("title"):
        return st["title"]
    joined = parts[0] if len(parts) == 1 else ", ".join(parts[:-1]) + " and " + parts[-1]
    if mains and all(m["role"] in _MINOR for m in mains):
        return f"{verb} the attaching parts"
    return f"{verb} {joined}"


def generate(process: dict, ipl: dict, kind: str, *, title: str, provider: LLMProvider | None = None,
             names: dict[str, str] | None = None, checker: STEChecker | None = None) -> dict:
    assert kind in ("assembly", "disassembly")
    provider = provider or NoneProvider()
    checker = checker or STEChecker(technical_names=technical_names_from(ipl, names))
    graph = process[kind]
    ops = {o["id"]: o for o in graph["operations"]}
    items_in_ipl = {r["item"] for r in ipl["rows"] if r.get("item")}
    safety = _safety(ipl)
    seal_rows = {r["id"] for r in ipl["rows"] if r["role"] in ("seal", "backup_ring")}
    spring_rows = {r["id"] for r in ipl["rows"] if r["role"] == "spring"}

    subtasks, all_steps = [], []
    for st in graph["subtasks"]:
        steps = []
        warn, caut = [], []
        for oid in st["ops"]:
            op = ops[oid]
            for k, sent in enumerate(sentences_for(op, names)):
                sid = f"{oid}-{k + 1}"
                step = {"id": sid, "text": sent["text"], "kind": sent["kind"], "op_ids": [oid],
                        "occ_ids": op.get("occ_ids", []), "rows": [i["row_id"] for i in op.get("items", [])],
                        "origin": "template", "flags": list(op.get("flags", []))}
                steps.append(step)
            rows_here = {i["row_id"] for i in op.get("items", [])} | {i["row_id"] for i in op.get("with", [])}
            for s in safety:
                if s["where"] == "spring" and rows_here & spring_rows and s["id"] not in warn:
                    warn.append(s["id"])
                if s["where"] == "seal_removal" and op["type"] in ("remove_from", "install_on") and rows_here & seal_rows \
                        and s["id"] not in caut:
                    caut.append(s["id"])
        subtasks.append({"id": st["id"], "title": _title(st, kind, ipl, names), "warnings": warn, "cautions": caut,
                         "steps": steps, "rows": st["rows"]})
        all_steps += steps

    seen_titles: dict[str, int] = {}
    for st in subtasks:
        t = st["title"]
        if t in seen_titles:
            st["title"] = t.replace("Remove the ", "Remove the remaining ").replace("Install the ", "Install the remaining ")
        seen_titles[t] = seen_titles.get(t, 0) + 1

    # optional wording improvement, guarded by the same checks
    usage = {}
    if provider.available() and all_steps:
        ctx = f"Procedure: {title}. Component: {(process.get('top') or {}).get('nomenclature', '')}."
        suggestions, usage = refine_steps(provider, [s for s in all_steps if s["kind"] == "step"], ctx,
                                         batch_size=getattr(provider, "batch_size", 12))
        for s in all_steps:
            new = suggestions.get(s["id"])
            if not new or new.strip() == s["text"]:
                continue
            op = ops[s["op_ids"][0]]
            if not [i for i in checker.check(new) + fact_check(new, op, items_in_ipl) if i["severity"] == "error"]:
                s["template_text"], s["text"], s["origin"] = s["text"], new.strip(), "llm"

    # checks
    counts = defaultdict(int)
    for s in all_steps:
        op = ops[s["op_ids"][0]]
        s["issues"] = checker.check(s["text"], s["kind"]) + fact_check(s["text"], op, items_in_ipl)
        for i in s["issues"]:
            counts[i["severity"]] += 1

    # preliminary requirements
    torques = [o["torque"] for o in graph["operations"] if o.get("torque")] if kind == "assembly" else []
    support = []
    for t in sorted(torques, key=lambda t: t["max_nm"]):
        name = wrench_for(t["max_nm"])
        if name not in [s["name"] for s in support]:
            support.append({"id": f"seq-{len(support) + 1:02d}", "name": name, "qty": 1, "source": "rule: torque range"})
    supplies, seen = [], set()
    for o in graph["operations"]:
        for s in o.get("supplies", []) or []:
            if s["spec"] not in seen and s["spec"] != "ATS":
                seen.add(s["spec"])
                supplies.append({"id": f"sup-{re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', s['spec'].lower())}", "spec": s["spec"],
                                 "name": supply_ref(s), "source": "drawing note"})
    general = process.get("general_notes", [])
    if kind == "assembly":
        for g in general:
            if g.get("op") != "apply_compound":
                continue
            for sp in g["specs"]:
                if sp not in seen:
                    seen.add(sp)
                    desc = next((x["description"] for x in ipl.get("supplies", []) if x["spec"] == sp), g["label"])
                    from ..process.graph import note_supply_name
                    nm = note_supply_name(g["text"], sp) or re.sub(r"(?i)\bprevent\.", "preventive", desc or "")
                    supplies.append({"id": f"sup-{re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', sp.lower())}", "spec": sp,
                                     "name": supply_ref({"spec": sp, "name": nm}), "source": "drawing note"})
    spares = []
    if kind == "assembly":
        for o in graph["operations"]:
            if o["type"] == "install_on" and o.get("new_items"):
                for it in o["items"]:
                    if it["row_id"] in o["new_items"]:
                        ex = next((s for s in spares if s["part_number"] == it["part_number"]), None)
                        if ex:
                            ex["qty"] += it.get("count") or 1
                        else:
                            spares.append({"id": f"spa-{re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', it['part_number'].lower())}",
                                           "part_number": it["part_number"], "name": clean_name(it, names),
                                           "item": it["item"], "qty": it.get("count") or 1})
    prelim_warn = [s for s in safety if s["where"] == "preliminary"]
    common = []
    if kind == "assembly":
        common = [f"{g['label']} ({', '.join(g['specs'])})." for g in general if g["specs"] and g.get("op") != "note"]
    proc = {
        "format": "studio.procedure/1", "kind": kind, "title": title,
        "component": process.get("top"),
        "common_info": common,
        "preliminary": {"persons": [{"category": "Shop technician", "count": 1}],
                        "support_equipment": support, "supplies": supplies, "spares": spares,
                        "warnings": [s["id"] for s in prelim_warn]},
        "safety": {s["id"]: {"kind": s["kind"], "text": s["text"], "source": s["source"], "evidence": s["evidence"]}
                   for s in safety},
        "subtasks": subtasks,
        "summary": {"subtasks": len(subtasks), "steps": len(all_steps), "errors": counts["error"],
                    "warnings": counts["warning"], "llm": provider.describe(), "usage": usage,
                    "llm_steps": sum(1 for s in all_steps if s["origin"] == "llm")},
    }
    return proc



================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\procedures\ste.py
================================================================================

"""ASD-STE100 checks and fact checks for generated procedure text.

Built-in rules (procedural writing) — each finding has a rule id, severity and a message:

* ``STE-4.1``  a procedural sentence has at most 20 words
* ``STE-8.1``  no semicolons
* ``STE-9.1``  an instruction starts with an approved verb in the imperative
* ``STE-MOD``  no modal verbs (should, could, may, might, would, shall)
* ``STE-ING``  no "-ing" verb forms (technical names excepted)
* ``STE-PAS``  no passive voice in instructions
* ``FACT-NUM`` every number in the text exists in the operation it came from (no invented values)
* ``FACT-ITM`` every item number in brackets exists in the IPL

Customer dictionaries plug in: ``STEChecker(extra_verbs=..., technical_names=...)``
(the same lists ASTHRA / TechPub keep per customer).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re

APPROVED_VERBS = {
    "adjust", "align", "apply", "attach", "bond", "cap", "clean", "close", "compress", "connect", "cover", "cut",
    "discard", "disconnect", "do", "drain", "dry", "engage", "examine", "fill", "hold", "identify", "install",
    "keep", "let", "loosen", "lubricate", "make", "measure", "monitor", "move", "open", "prepare", "pull", "push",
    "put", "record", "refer", "release", "remove", "replace", "safety", "set", "tighten", "torque", "turn", "use",
    "wipe", "after", "before", "if", "when", "for", "with", "note", "warning", "caution",
}
ING_OK = {"packing", "packings", "ring", "rings", "bushing", "bushings", "fitting", "fittings", "spring", "springs",
          "housing", "housings", "bearing", "bearings", "coating", "anodising", "anodizing", "o-ring", "back-up",
          "during", "thing", "things", "string", "following", "opening", "openings", "marking", "markings",
          "filling", "anything", "nothing", "something", "everything", "drawing", "drawings", "testing",
          # technical modifiers in part names ("retaining ring", "locking washer", "closing spacer")
          "retaining", "locking", "sealing", "mounting", "adjusting", "closing", "machining", "centering",
          "centring", "guiding", "damping", "backing", "bearing", "padding", "lining", "casting", "forging",
          "mooring", "tubing", "piping", "wiring", "shielding", "spacing", "fixing", "clamping", "coupling",
          "couplings", "landing", "steering", "folding", "reclining", "swivelling", "tracking", "stiffening"}


def technical_names_from(ipl: dict | None, names: dict | None = None) -> set[str]:
    """-ing words that are part of a part's name in this IPL ('recopy lever machining'): not verb forms."""
    out: set[str] = set()
    texts = [r.get("nomenclature") or "" for r in (ipl or {}).get("rows", [])] + list((names or {}).values())
    for t in texts:
        for w in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]*ing\b", str(t)):
            out.add(w.lower())
    return out
MODALS = {"should", "could", "may", "might", "would", "shall", "must"}
NUMBER_WORDS = {"one": 1, "two": 2, "three": 3, "four": 4, "five": 5, "six": 6, "seven": 7, "eight": 8, "nine": 9, "ten": 10}


class STEChecker:
    def __init__(self, extra_verbs: set[str] | None = None, technical_names: set[str] | None = None,
                 max_words: int = 20, max_words_descriptive: int = 25):
        self.verbs = APPROVED_VERBS | {v.lower() for v in (extra_verbs or set())}
        self.names = {n.lower() for n in (technical_names or set())}
        self.max_words = max_words
        self.max_words_descriptive = max_words_descriptive

    def check(self, text: str, kind: str = "step") -> list[dict]:
        issues = []
        sentences = [s.strip() for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", text.strip()) if s.strip()]
        for s in sentences:
            core = re.sub(r"\([^)]*\)", "", s)                       # item refs and specs do not count as words
            words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z\-']*", core)
            if kind == "step" and len(words) > self.max_words:
                issues.append({"rule": "STE-4.1", "severity": "error",
                               "message": f"{len(words)} words; a procedural sentence has at most {self.max_words}."})
            elif kind != "step" and len(words) > self.max_words_descriptive:
                issues.append({"rule": "STE-4.2", "severity": "error",
                               "message": f"{len(words)} words; a descriptive sentence has at most {self.max_words_descriptive}."})
            if ";" in s:
                issues.append({"rule": "STE-8.1", "severity": "error", "message": "Do not use semicolons."})
            if kind == "step" and words:
                first = words[0].lower()
                if first not in self.verbs and not s.lower().startswith(("do not", "make sure")):
                    issues.append({"rule": "STE-9.1", "severity": "warning",
                                   "message": f"Start an instruction with an approved verb (found '{words[0]}')."})
            for w in words:
                lw = w.lower()
                if lw in MODALS:
                    issues.append({"rule": "STE-MOD", "severity": "error", "message": f"Do not use '{w}'."})
                if lw.endswith("ing") and len(lw) > 4 and lw not in ING_OK and lw not in self.names:
                    issues.append({"rule": "STE-ING", "severity": "warning",
                                   "message": f"Avoid the -ing form '{w}' unless it is a technical name."})
            if kind == "step" and re.search(r"\b(is|are|be|been)\s+\w+ed\b", core, re.I):
                issues.append({"rule": "STE-PAS", "severity": "warning", "message": "Use the active voice in instructions."})
        return issues


def _numbers(text: str) -> list[str]:
    t = re.sub(r"\b[A-Z]{2,}[A-Z0-9]*-[A-Z0-9\-]+\b", " ", text)       # spec codes like PCS-7200, IFC30-145-07
    t = re.sub(r"\b[A-Z]+\d+[A-Z0-9\-]*\b", " ", t)
    return re.findall(r"(?<![\w.])-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?[A-Z]?", t)


def allowed_numbers(op: dict) -> set[str]:
    nums: set[str] = set()

    def add(v):
        if v is None:
            return
        if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
            s = f"{v:.2f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".") if isinstance(v, float) else str(v)
            nums.add(s)
        else:
            nums.add(str(v))
    for key in ("items", "with", "on_items"):
        for it in op.get(key) or []:
            add(it.get("item"))
            add(it.get("count"))
            add(it.get("qty"))
    for key in ("from", "on"):
        if op.get(key):
            add(op[key].get("item"))
    if op.get("torque"):
        for k in ("min_nm", "max_nm", "min_lbfin", "max_lbfin", "nominal_nm"):
            add(float(op["torque"][k]))
    for key in ("supplies", "references"):
        for sp in op.get(key) or []:
            for n in re.findall(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?", f"{sp.get('name', '')} {sp.get('description', '')} {sp.get('spec', '')}"):
                nums.add(n)
    return nums


def fact_check(text: str, op: dict, ipl_items: set[str]) -> list[dict]:
    issues = []
    allowed = allowed_numbers(op)
    for n in _numbers(text):
        if n not in allowed and n.rstrip("0").rstrip(".") not in allowed:
            issues.append({"rule": "FACT-NUM", "severity": "error",
                           "message": f"'{n}' is not a value of this operation (item, quantity or torque)."})
    refs = [x.strip() for grp in re.findall(r"\((-?\d+[A-Z]?(?:,\s*-?\d+[A-Z]?)*)\)", text) for x in grp.split(",")]
    for it in refs:
        if it not in ipl_items:
            issues.append({"rule": "FACT-ITM", "severity": "error", "message": f"Item ({it}) is not in the IPL."})
    for w, v in NUMBER_WORDS.items():
        if re.search(rf"\b{w}\b", text, re.I) and str(v) not in allowed:
            issues.append({"rule": "FACT-NUM", "severity": "error",
                           "message": f"Quantity '{w}' does not match this operation."})
    return issues

"""STE sentences for process operations (ASD-STE100 style).

Deterministic templates: one instruction per sentence, approved verbs at the start
(REMOVE, INSTALL, DISCARD, TORQUE, APPLY, SAFETY, DO, MAKE SURE), at most 20 words,
item numbers in parentheses, quantities in words up to ten, torque in N.m with lbf.in.

Names come from the IPL nomenclature reduced to the basic noun phrase a technician reads
("SCREW NAS1351N4-20 .2500-28UNRF" -> "screw"; "VALVE, PILOT SOLENOID" -> "pilot solenoid
valve"). Projects can override names per part number (``names`` in the procedure options).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re

WORDS = {1: "one", 2: "two", 3: "three", 4: "four", 5: "five", 6: "six", 7: "seven", 8: "eight", 9: "nine", 10: "ten"}
ROLE_NOUN = {"fastener": "screw", "washer": "washer", "nut": "nut", "seal": "packing", "backup_ring": "back-up ring",
             "insert": "insert", "press_plug": "expansion plug", "cap": "protective cap", "lockwire": "safety cable",
             "spring": "spring", "bush": "bush"}
IRREGULAR = {"bush": "bushes", "packing": "packings", "body": "bodies", "assembly": "assemblies"}


def plural(noun: str) -> str:
    last = noun.split()[-1]
    if last in IRREGULAR:
        return noun[: -len(last)] + IRREGULAR[last]
    if last.endswith(("s", "x", "ch", "sh")):
        return noun + "es"
    if last.endswith("y") and last[-2:-1] not in "aeiou":
        return noun[:-1] + "ies"
    return noun + "s"


def qty_word(n: int | None) -> str:
    if not n:
        return ""
    return WORDS.get(n, str(n))


def clean_name(item: dict, names: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str:
    """Basic noun phrase for running text."""
    names = names or {}
    if item.get("part_number") in names:
        return names[item["part_number"]]
    role = item.get("role")
    nom = (item.get("nomenclature") or "").upper()
    if role in ("fastener",) and re.search(r"\bBOLT\b", nom):
        return "bolt"
    if role == "seal":
        if "O RING" in nom or "O-RING" in nom or "PACKING" in nom:
            return "packing"
        if "DYNAMIC" in nom:
            return "dynamic seal"
        return "seal"
    if role in ROLE_NOUN and role not in ("cap",):
        return ROLE_NOUN[role]
    # "VALVE, PILOT SOLENOID" -> "pilot solenoid valve"; drop part numbers / thread specs
    parts = [p.strip() for p in nom.split(",")]
    phrase = " ".join(parts[1:] + parts[:1]) if len(parts) > 1 else parts[0]
    toks = [t for t in phrase.split() if not re.search(r"\d", t) and t not in ("WITH", "PNR", "ASSY")]
    phrase = " ".join(toks).lower().replace("equiped", "equipped")
    if role == "housing" and phrase == "body equipped":
        phrase = "equipped body"
    if phrase in ("bague",):
        phrase = "bush"
    return phrase or (item.get("step_name") or "part").lower()


def group_ref(items: list[dict], names: dict | None = None) -> str:
    """Parts of the same kind together: 'the inserts (160, 350, 400) and the expansion plugs (380, 390)'.
    For long lists (notes about parts that stay installed); quantities are left to the IPL."""
    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for it in items:
        groups.setdefault(clean_name(it, names), []).append(str(it["item"]))
    out = []
    for noun, nums in groups.items():
        many = len(nums) > 1 or any((it.get("count") or it.get("qty") or 1) > 1 for it in items if clean_name(it, names) == noun)
        out.append(f"the {plural(noun) if many else noun} ({', '.join(nums)})")
    return out[0] if len(out) == 1 else ", ".join(out[:-1]) + " and " + out[-1]


def ref(items: list[dict], names: dict | None = None, the: bool = True) -> str:
    """'the six screws (220) and the six washers (230)'"""
    out = []
    for it in items:
        n = it.get("count") or it.get("qty") or 1
        noun = clean_name(it, names)
        noun = plural(noun) if n > 1 else noun
        q = qty_word(n) if n > 1 else ""
        art = "the " if the else ""
        out.append(f"{art}{q + ' ' if q else ''}{noun} ({it['item']})")
    if len(out) <= 1:
        return out[0] if out else ""
    return ", ".join(out[:-1]) + " and " + out[-1]


def torque_text(t: dict) -> str:
    if t["min_nm"] == t["max_nm"]:
        return f"{_n(t['min_nm'])} N.m ({_n(t['min_lbfin'])} lbf.in)"
    return f"{_n(t['min_nm'])} to {_n(t['max_nm'])} N.m ({_n(t['min_lbfin'])} to {_n(t['max_lbfin'])} lbf.in)"


def _n(v: float) -> str:
    return f"{v:.2f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".") if isinstance(v, float) else str(v)


def target(it: dict | None, names: dict | None = None) -> str:
    """'the plugs (210)' — plural when the operation acts on several of them."""
    if not it:
        return ""
    n = it.get("count") or 1
    noun = clean_name(it, names)
    return f"the {plural(noun) if n > 1 else noun} ({it['item']})"


def new_ref(items: list[dict], names: dict | None = None) -> str:
    """'two new packings (260)' / 'a new dynamic seal (300)'"""
    out = []
    for it in items:
        n = it.get("count") or 1
        noun = clean_name(it, names)
        out.append(f"{qty_word(n)} new {plural(noun)} ({it['item']})" if n > 1 else f"a new {noun} ({it['item']})")
    return out[0] if len(out) == 1 else ", ".join(out[:-1]) + " and " + out[-1]


def supply_ref(s: dict) -> str:
    if s.get("name"):
        return f"{s['name'].strip().lower()} ({s['spec']})"
    d = (s.get("description") or s.get("name") or "").strip().lower()
    d = re.sub(r"\bprevent\.", "preventive", d)
    return f"{d} ({s['spec']})" if d else s["spec"]


MAX_WORDS = 20


def _words(t: str) -> int:
    return len(t.split())


def new_group_ref(items: list[dict], names: dict | None = None) -> str:
    """'new packings (750, 490) and new back-up rings (100, 760)' — quantities are left to the IPL."""
    groups: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for it in items:
        groups.setdefault(clean_name(it, names), []).append(it)
    out = []
    for noun, its in groups.items():
        many = len(its) > 1 or any((i.get("count") or 1) > 1 for i in its)
        out.append(f"new {plural(noun)} ({', '.join(str(i['item']) for i in its)})" if many
                   else f"a new {noun} ({its[0]['item']})")
    return out[0] if len(out) == 1 else ", ".join(out[:-1]) + " and " + out[-1]


def item_sentences(verb: str, items: list[dict], tail: str = "", names: dict | None = None,
                   new: bool = False) -> list[str]:
    """'Remove the six screws (220) and the washers (230) from the cover (10).' — and for long lists,
    the same kinds together, split into several sentences so each keeps to the STE length (20 words)."""
    if not items:
        return []
    one_ref, grp_ref = (new_ref, new_group_ref) if new else (ref, group_ref)
    one = f"{verb} {one_ref(items, names)}{tail}."
    if len(items) <= 3 and _words(one) <= MAX_WORDS:
        return [one]
    grouped = f"{verb} {grp_ref(items, names)}{tail}."
    if _words(grouped) <= MAX_WORDS:
        return [grouped]
    kinds: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for it in items:
        kinds.setdefault(clean_name(it, names), []).append(it)
    out, cur = [], []
    for grp in kinds.values():
        trial = cur + grp
        if cur and _words(f"{verb} {grp_ref(trial, names)}{tail}.") > MAX_WORDS:
            out.append(f"{verb} {grp_ref(cur, names)}{tail}.")
            cur = list(grp)
        else:
            cur = trial
    if cur:
        out.append(f"{verb} {grp_ref(cur, names)}{tail}.")
    return out


def sentences_for(op: dict, names: dict | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Return [{text, kind}] for one operation. kind: step | note | warning | caution."""
    t = op["type"]
    items = op.get("items", [])
    out: list[dict] = []
    frm = op.get("from")
    on = op.get("on")
    plural_items = sum((i.get("count") or 1) for i in items) > 1 or len(items) > 1
    them = "them" if plural_items else "it"
    if t == "unfasten":
        tgt = f" from {target(frm, names)}" if frm else ""
        out += [{"text": x, "kind": "step"} for x in item_sentences("Remove", items, tgt, names)]
    elif t == "remove":
        tgt = f" from {target(frm, names)}" if frm else ""
        out += [{"text": x, "kind": "step"} for x in item_sentences("Remove", items, tgt, names)]
        if op.get("discard"):
            out += [{"text": x, "kind": "step"} for x in item_sentences("Discard", items, "", names)]
    elif t == "remove_from":
        out += [{"text": x, "kind": "step"} for x in item_sentences("Remove", items, f" from {target(frm, names)}", names)]
        disc = [i for i in items if i["row_id"] in op.get("discard_items", [])]
        if disc:
            out += [{"text": x, "kind": "step"} for x in item_sentences("Discard", disc, "", names)]
    elif t == "do_not_remove":
        what = ref(items, names) if len(items) <= 2 else group_ref(items, names)
        out.append({"text": f"Do not remove {what} {op.get('condition', '')}.".replace("  ", " ").replace(" .", "."),
                    "kind": "note"})
    elif t == "do_not_disassemble":
        what = ref(items, names) if len(items) <= 3 else group_ref(items, names)
        out.append({"text": f"Do not disassemble {what} further.", "kind": "note"})
    elif t == "install_on":
        new = [i for i in items if i["row_id"] in op.get("new_items", [])]
        rest = [i for i in items if i not in new]
        if new:
            out += [{"text": x, "kind": "step"} for x in item_sentences("Install", new, f" on {target(on, names)}", names, new=True)]
        if rest:
            out += [{"text": x, "kind": "step"} for x in item_sentences("Install", rest, f" on {target(on, names)}", names)]
    elif t == "install":
        tgt = f" in {target(on, names)}" if on else ""
        out += [{"text": x, "kind": "step"} for x in item_sentences("Install", items, tgt, names, new=bool(op.get("new_parts")))]
        for r in op.get("references") or []:
            out.append({"text": f"Refer to {r['spec']} for the installation.", "kind": "step"})
        if op.get("torque"):
            out.append({"text": f"Torque {ref(items, names)} to {torque_text(op['torque'])}.", "kind": "step"})
    elif t == "fasten":
        sup = op.get("supplies") or []
        if sup:
            out.append({"text": f"Apply {supply_ref(sup[0])} to {ref(items, names)}.", "kind": "step"})
        if on:
            out.append({"text": f"Attach {target(on, names)} with {ref(items, names)}.", "kind": "step"})
        else:
            out.append({"text": f"Install {ref(items, names)}.", "kind": "step"})
        if op.get("torque"):
            fast = [i for i in items if i["role"] in ("fastener", "nut")] or items[:1]
            out.append({"text": f"Torque {ref(fast, names)} to {torque_text(op['torque'])}.", "kind": "step"})
    elif t == "apply":
        sup = (op.get("supplies") or [{}])[0]
        its = op.get("on_items") or []
        heads = [i for i in its if i["role"] in ("fastener", "nut")]
        rest = [i for i in its if i not in heads]
        where = []
        if heads:
            where.append("on the heads of " + ref([{**i, "count": 0} for i in heads], names))
        if rest:
            where.append("on " + ref([{**i, "count": 0} for i in rest], names))
        what = supply_ref(sup) if sup else op.get("what", "sealant")
        out.append({"text": f"Apply {what} {' and '.join(where)}.".replace("  ", " "), "kind": "step"})
    elif t == "lockwire":
        spec = ", ".join(op.get("spec") or [])
        out.append({"text": f"Safety the parts shown on the drawing with lock wire or safety cable ({spec}).", "kind": "step"})
    elif t == "test":
        out.append({"text": "Do the acceptance test procedure (ATS).", "kind": "step"})
    elif t == "apply_after_test":
        spec = ", ".join(op.get("spec") or [])
        its = op.get("items") or []
        where = f"the holes of {ref(its, names)}" if its else "the Lee plug holes"
        out.append({"text": f"After the test, fill {where} with thick sealant ({spec}).", "kind": "step"})
    else:
        out.append({"text": op.get("text") or t, "kind": "note"})
    return out

================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\process\graph.py
