"""
Canonical MBOM field -> list of header text variants that map to it.

This is intentionally kept separate from the loading/matching logic. If a
different BOM format shows up (different column names, different provider),
extend this dict rather than touching mbom_loader.py or reconciler.py.

Matching against actual header text is done case-insensitively and after
stripping whitespace/newlines (PDF-extracted headers often come back with
embedded newlines from vertically-stacked column labels, e.g. "L\\ne\\nv").
"""

DEFAULT_COLUMN_MAP = {
    "level": ["Lev", "Level", "Lev v", "Niveau"],
    "find_number": ["Find Number", "FindNumber", "Find No", "Find No."],
    "seq_number": ["Seq. Number", "Seq Number", "Sequence", "Seq No", "Seq"],
    "equiv": ["Equiv", "Equivalence"],
    "part_number": ["Part Number", "PN", "Part No", "Part No.", "REF_ARTICLE", "Article", "Code Article"],
    # Explicit CAD/3D model cross-reference field, distinct from the
    # manufacturing part number — confirmed real case: a production MBOM
    # had BOTH "REF_ARTICLE" (the manufacturing part number, populated on
    # every row) AND "Reference du 3D" (only populated on some rows,
    # specifically meant to record the corresponding CAD/3D reference) as
    # separate columns. Kept separate rather than conflated.
    "cad_reference": ["Reference du 3D", "Ref 3D", "3D Reference"],
    "amdt": ["Amdt", "Amendment", "Révision", "Revision"],
    "description": ["Description", "Nomenclature", "Désignation FR", "Désignation EN"],
    "qty": ["Qty.", "Qty", "Quantity", "Quantité(L)", "Quantité", "Qté/SS"],
    "unit_measure": ["Unit Measure", "UOM", "Unit", "Unité de mesure(L)"],
    "material_spec": ["Material Specification", "Material Spec", "Material", "MATIERE_GENERIQUE"],
    "comments": ["Comments", "Comment", "Remarks", "Notes"],
    "class": ["Class", "TYPE_COMPOSANT"],
    "manuf_code": ["Manuf. Code", "Manufacturer Code", "Manuf Code", "CAGE", "CAGE Code"],
    "status": ["Status", "Etat", "État"],
    "authority": ["Authority"],
}

def get_template_headers() -> list:
    """One clean, canonical header string per recognized field — the
    exact text a user's own spreadsheet should use for guaranteed clean
    parsing, bypassing all the format-detection/inference logic needed
    for arbitrary real-world exports."""
    return [variants[0] for variants in DEFAULT_COLUMN_MAP.values()]


def normalize_header_text(text) -> str:
    """Collapses PDF-extracted vertical-text headers like 'L\\ne\\nv' -> 'lev',
    and normal headers like 'Manuf. Code' -> 'manuf. code', for matching."""
    if text is None:
        return ""
    return "".join(str(text).split()).lower().strip()


def build_index_map(header_row: list, column_map: dict = None) -> dict:
    """Given a raw header row (list of cell values, possibly with None gaps
    and embedded newlines), returns {canonical_field: column_index}.

    Only fields actually found in this header row are included — callers
    should treat missing fields as "not available in this document" rather
    than erroring, since not every MBOM export has every column.
    """
    column_map = column_map or DEFAULT_COLUMN_MAP
    normalized_variants = {
        canonical: {normalize_header_text(v) for v in variants}
        for canonical, variants in column_map.items()
    }

    result = {}
    for idx, cell in enumerate(header_row):
        norm = normalize_header_text(cell)
        if not norm:
            continue
        for canonical, variants in normalized_variants.items():
            if norm in variants and canonical not in result:
                result[canonical] = idx
                break
    return result




================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\reconcile\mbom_loader.py
================================================================================

"""
Loads an MBOM/APL document from either Excel/CSV or PDF into a common list
of dicts, using column_mapping.py to identify fields regardless of exact
header wording or column order.

Returns: list[dict], each dict having whatever canonical fields were found
(level, part_number, description, qty, manuf_code, comments, ...).
Missing fields are simply absent from the dict, not filled with None,
so downstream code should use .get() with sensible defaults.
"""

import re
from pathlib import Path
from .column_mapping import build_index_map, DEFAULT_COLUMN_MAP


def _clean_cell(value) -> str:
    if value is None:
        return ""
    # pandas represents empty Excel cells as float NaN, not None — str(nan)
    # is the literal string "nan", which is truthy and was corrupting every
    # sheet's data (empty cells counted as real values) until this check
    # was added. Confirmed real bug on an actual multi-sheet Excel workbook,
    # not present with the PDF loader since pdfplumber returns real None
    # for missing cells instead.
    try:
        import math
        if isinstance(value, float) and math.isnan(value):
            return ""
    except TypeError:
        pass
    return str(value).strip()

def load_from_pasted_text(text: str, column_map: dict = None) -> list:
    """Parses tabular data pasted directly by a user (e.g. copied from
    Excel) — tab-separated by default (Excel's actual clipboard format),
    falling back to comma-separated if no tabs are found at all. Reuses
    the same header-detection/row-parsing logic as the file-based
    loaders, tested directly against both delimiter styles.
    """
    column_map = column_map or DEFAULT_COLUMN_MAP
    raw_lines = [line for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    if not raw_lines:
        raise ValueError("No data found in pasted text.")

    delimiter = "\t" if "\t" in raw_lines[0] else ","
    rows = [line.split(delimiter) for line in raw_lines]

    header_row_idx = None
    for i, row in enumerate(rows[:10]):
        if _looks_like_header_row(row, column_map):
            header_row_idx = i
            break
    if header_row_idx is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "Could not find a header row with a recognizable Part Number "
            "column in the pasted data. Make sure the first row (or one "
            "of the first few) contains column headers, or use the "
            "downloadable template for guaranteed formatting."
        )

    index_map = build_index_map(rows[header_row_idx], column_map)
    records = []
    for row in rows[header_row_idx + 1:]:
        rec = _row_to_record(row, index_map)
        if rec.get("part_number"):
            records.append(rec)
    return records

def _row_to_record(row: list, index_map: dict) -> dict:
    record = {}
    for field, idx in index_map.items():
        if idx < len(row):
            val = _clean_cell(row[idx])
            if val:
                record[field] = val
    return record


def _looks_like_header_row(row: list, column_map: dict) -> bool:
    idx_map = build_index_map(row, column_map)
    # Require part_number AND at least one other real BOM field —
    # confirmed real case: a row containing only a "Code Article" cell
    # (matching part_number alone) sat above the actual header row in a
    # real multi-block Excel sheet, and got wrongly accepted as the
    # header when only part_number was required. That misaligned every
    # column for every row below it, including the real header row.
    if "part_number" not in idx_map:
        return False
    return any(f in idx_map for f in ("description", "qty"))


def load_from_excel_or_csv(path: str, column_map: dict = None, sheet_name: str = None) -> list:
    """sheet_name: force a specific sheet. If omitted, every sheet is
    scanned and the best-scoring one is used automatically.

    Confirmed necessary on a real 19-sheet production workbook: most
    sheets are NOT flat BOM tables at all (wide per-seat-position
    quantity matrices, packaging lists, workstation timing sheets), and
    sheet NAMING is not reliable either — a sheet named "EBOM report
    23-09" in that file turned out to be a manufacturing timing extract,
    not a BOM, despite the name strongly suggesting otherwise. Only
    scoring actual header content per sheet catches this correctly.
    """
    import pandas as pd

    column_map = column_map or DEFAULT_COLUMN_MAP
    path_obj = Path(path)
    is_csv = path_obj.suffix.lower() == ".csv"

    if is_csv:
        sheets = {"__csv__": pd.read_csv(path, header=None).values.tolist()}
    elif sheet_name:
        sheets = {sheet_name: pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name=sheet_name, header=None).values.tolist()}
    else:
        xls = pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name=None, header=None)
        sheets = {name: df.values.tolist() for name, df in xls.items()}

    best_name, best_records, best_field_count, best_row_count = None, [], -1, -1

    for name, rows in sheets.items():
        header_row_idx = None
        for i, row in enumerate(rows[:20]):  # header may sit deeper than 10 rows in multi-block sheets
            if _looks_like_header_row(row, column_map):
                header_row_idx = i
                break
        if header_row_idx is None:
            continue

        index_map = build_index_map(rows[header_row_idx], column_map)
        records = []
        for row in rows[header_row_idx + 1:]:
            rec = _row_to_record(row, index_map)
            if rec.get("part_number"):
                records.append(rec)

        # Primary score: how many distinct canonical fields the header
        # recognized — richer header = more likely a real BOM export, not
        # a derived report. Row count is only a tiebreaker. Confirmed
        # necessary: a per-seat-position "matrix" sheet naturally has far
        # MORE rows than the actual hierarchical EBOM (every component
        # repeats once per seat position), so row count alone picked the
        # wrong sheet even though it had fewer distinct recognized fields
        # (4 vs the real EBOM sheet's 5, including "level" — which
        # matrix-style sheets never have at all).
        field_count = len(index_map)
        row_count = len(records)
        if (field_count, row_count) > (best_field_count, best_row_count):
            best_name, best_records = name, records
            best_field_count, best_row_count = field_count, row_count

    if best_row_count <= 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "Could not find a header row with a recognizable Part Number "
            "column on any sheet. Check column_mapping.py — the actual "
            "header text in this file may need a variant added, or pass "
            "sheet_name explicitly if you know which sheet has the BOM."
        )

    return best_records


def load_from_pdf(path: str, column_map: dict = None) -> list:
    """Best-effort PDF table extraction via pdfplumber. Column POSITION
    (not just header text) is used to align data rows to fields.

    IMPORTANT: the header row is re-detected independently on EVERY page,
    not just once for the whole document. Confirmed against a real 3-page
    Safran APL report that different pages can have different column
    counts/layouts even within the same document. Reusing one page's
    index map on another page's rows silently misaligns every field —
    this must not be "optimized" into a single global header detection.

    Recommend spot-checking the first run's output against the source PDF
    for any new BOM format before trusting it fully — PDF table extraction
    quality varies by exporting tool.
    """
    import pdfplumber

    column_map = column_map or DEFAULT_COLUMN_MAP
    records = []
    pages_with_no_header = []

    with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:
        for page_num, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1):
            tables = page.extract_tables()
            for table in tables:
                index_map = None
                for row in table:
                    if index_map is None:
                        if _looks_like_header_row(row, column_map):
                            index_map = build_index_map(row, column_map)
                        continue
                    rec = _row_to_record(row, index_map)
                    if rec.get("part_number"):
                        records.append(rec)
                if index_map is None:
                    pages_with_no_header.append(page_num)

    if not records:
        raise ValueError(
            "Could not find a header row with a recognizable Part Number "
            "column anywhere in the PDF tables. This BOM format may need "
            "a new header variant added to column_mapping.py, or the PDF's "
            "table structure may not be extractable by pdfplumber at all "
            "(e.g. a scanned/image-based PDF, which would need OCR first)."
        )
    if pages_with_no_header:
        import warnings
        warnings.warn(
            f"No header row found on page(s) {pages_with_no_header} — "
            f"any data rows on those pages were skipped entirely rather "
            f"than risk misaligned fields. Spot-check those pages manually."
        )

    return records


def load_mbom(path: str, column_map: dict = None, sheet_name: str = None) -> list:
    """Auto-detects format by extension and loads accordingly.
    sheet_name only applies to .xlsx/.xls — ignored/irrelevant for .csv/.pdf.
    """
    suffix = Path(path).suffix.lower()
    if suffix in (".xlsx", ".xls", ".csv"):
        return load_from_excel_or_csv(path, column_map, sheet_name)
    elif suffix == ".pdf":
        return load_from_pdf(path, column_map)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MBOM file type: {suffix}. Expected .xlsx, .xls, .csv, or .pdf")


def strip_hierarchy_dots(part_number: str) -> tuple:
    """Some MBOM exports (confirmed on a real Safran APL) prefix part
    numbers with leading dots indicating hierarchy depth, e.g. '..C75970'
    for a level-2 item. Returns (clean_part_number, dot_count) so dot_count
    can be used as a redundant cross-check against an explicit Level column
    when both are present. Returns dot_count=0 for part numbers using a
    different depth convention — see get_hierarchy_depth for the unified
    entry point.
    """
    match = re.match(r"^(\.*)(.*)$", part_number)
    dots, clean = match.group(1), match.group(2)
    return clean.strip(), len(dots)


def get_hierarchy_depth(record: dict) -> int:
    """Unified depth extraction across the two conventions seen so far:
    - Leading dots directly on the part number (Safran APL PDF format)
    - A separate 'level' column using asterisks, e.g. '**' = depth 2
      (confirmed real case: a French production EBOM export using
      Niveau='*'/'**'/'***' instead of encoding depth into the part
      number string at all)

    Extend here, not by guessing in structural_context.py, if a third
    convention shows up — this is the one place depth interpretation
    should live.
    """
    pn = record.get("part_number", "")
    _, dot_depth = strip_hierarchy_dots(pn)
    if dot_depth > 0:
        return dot_depth

    level_raw = record.get("level", "")
    if level_raw and set(level_raw.strip()) == {"*"}:
        return len(level_raw.strip())

    try:
        return int(float(level_raw))
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return 0




================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\reconcile\nomenclature.py
================================================================================

"""
Lightweight, mostly-dependency-free nomenclature comparison, plus an
optional offline cross-lingual layer for cases where STEP and MBOM
nomenclature are in different languages (confirmed real case: French
part descriptions in a Safran MBOM, e.g. "STATOR RECTIFIE").

Design: a small curated glossary (precise, zero risk of confidently-wrong
output) is checked first, then offline machine translation (argos-translate)
fills in whatever the glossary doesn't cover — auto-expanding coverage
without hand-maintaining every word. Deliberately offline, not a cloud
API: this pipeline processes proprietary aerospace nomenclature, and
sending that to a third-party translation service on every match attempt
is not a decision to make silently.

Both layers degrade gracefully to "no signal" if unavailable — this must
never break the matching pipeline. A missing translation just means this
one signal contributes nothing to that comparison.
"""

import re
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger("bom_reconciliation.nomenclature")

# --- Same-language normalization (unchanged from earlier) ------------------

NORMALIZATION_RULES = [
    (re.compile(r"\bSCREWLOCK\b"), "SCREW LOCK"),
    (re.compile(r"\bTANGFREE\b"), "TANG FREE"),
    (re.compile(r"\bTANGLESS\b"), "TANG LESS"),
]

STOPWORDS = {"OF", "THE", "FOR", "TO", "A", "AN"}


def _stem(word: str) -> str:
    if len(word) <= 3:
        return word
    if word.endswith("IES"):
        return word[:-3] + "Y"
    if word.endswith("ES") and word[-3] not in "AEIOU":
        return word[:-2]
    if word.endswith("S") and not word.endswith("SS"):
        return word[:-1]
    return word


def normalize_and_tokenize(text: str) -> set:
    if not text:
        return set()
    text = text.upper().strip()
    for pattern, replacement in NORMALIZATION_RULES:
        text = pattern.sub(replacement, text)
    text = re.sub(r"[,\-/]", " ", text)
    tokens = [t for t in text.split() if t and t not in STOPWORDS]
    return {_stem(t) for t in tokens}


def token_similarity(name_a: str, name_b: str) -> float:
    tokens_a = normalize_and_tokenize(name_a)
    tokens_b = normalize_and_tokenize(name_b)
    if not tokens_a or not tokens_b:
        return 0.0
    intersection = tokens_a & tokens_b
    union = tokens_a | tokens_b
    return len(intersection) / len(union)

# Common leading "type" nouns seen across real MBOM/STEP nomenclature in
# this project so far. Best-effort category signal, NOT a rigorous
# taxonomy — e.g. "SCREW, CAP, SOCKET HEAD" and "SCREW NAS1351N4-20" both
# resolve to type SCREW even though the rest of the phrase differs
# completely. Extend only when a real mismatch demonstrates the need.

KNOWN_COMPONENT_TYPES = {
    "SCREW", "WASHER", "SEAL", "RING", "SPRING", "VALVE", "PLUG", "INSERT",
    "PIN", "BOLT", "NUT", "BUSH", "BUSHING", "PLATE", "CAP", "COVER",
    "HOUSING", "BODY", "SHAFT", "GASKET", "BEARING", "CLAMP", "SLEEVE",
    "PISTON", "ROTOR", "STATOR", "MAGNET", "COIL", "WIRE", "CABLE",
    "BRACKET", "PACKING", "ASSEMBLY", "BOBBIN",
}

# Checked BEFORE the generic single-word bucket below. Confirmed real
# false-positive: "O-RING" and "BACK-UP RING" both reduced to the same
# generic "RING" type, causing the scorer to treat an O-ring and a
# back-up ring — genuinely different components, even though they're
# often installed as a pair — as an exact component-type match.
COMPOUND_TYPE_RULES = [
    ({"O", "RING"}, "O-RING"),
    ({"BACK", "RING"}, "BACK-UP-RING"),
    ({"RETAINING", "RING"}, "RETAINING-RING"),
    ({"SNAP", "RING"}, "SNAP-RING"),
]


def extract_component_type(text):
    tokens = normalize_and_tokenize(text)
    for required_tokens, type_name in COMPOUND_TYPE_RULES:
        if required_tokens <= tokens:
            return type_name
    for t in tokens:
        if t in KNOWN_COMPONENT_TYPES:
            return t
    return None


def component_type_match(name_a, name_b):
    """0.0 if either side has no recognized type word — treated as 'no
    signal available', not as a mismatch, so this never falsely drags a
    score down just because our keyword list is incomplete.
    """
    type_a = extract_component_type(name_a)
    type_b = extract_component_type(name_b)
    if type_a is None or type_b is None:
        return 0.0
    return 1.0 if type_a == type_b else 0.0

# --- Curated glossary --------------------------------------------------------

# Seeded only from vocabulary confirmed present in real MBOM/STEP data this
# pipeline has actually processed (F6137-D24903000, F6137-D24907000).
# Extend only when a real cross-language mismatch demonstrates the need.
FR_EN_GLOSSARY = {
    "STATOR": "STATOR",
    "ROTOR": "ROTOR",
    "BOBINE": "COIL",
    "AIMANT": "MAGNET",
    "VIS": "SCREW",
    "RONDELLE": "WASHER",
    "JOINT": "SEAL",
    "RESSORT": "SPRING",
    "PLAQUE": "PLATE",
    "CORPS": "BODY",
    "AXE": "SHAFT",
    "CULASSE": "HEAD",
    "COUVERCLE": "COVER",
    "ECROU": "NUT",
    "GOUPILLE": "PIN",
    "BAGUE": "RING",
    "FIL": "WIRE",
    "FILS": "WIRES",
    "BOITIER": "HOUSING",
    "RECTIFIE": "GROUND",
    "RECTIFIEE": "GROUND",
    "USINAGE": "MACHINING",
    "USINE": "MACHINED",
    "EMBASE": "BASE",
    "BOUCHON": "PLUG",
    "CAPUCHON": "CAP",
    "COLLIER": "CLAMP",
    "DOUILLE": "SLEEVE",
    "SIEGE": "SEAT",
    "ENSEMBLE": "ASSEMBLY",
    "SUPPORT": "SUPPORT",
    "VALVE": "VALVE",
    "PISTON": "PISTON",
    "CABLE": "CABLE",
    "PRECHARGE": "PRELOAD",
}

EN_FR_GLOSSARY = {v: k for k, v in FR_EN_GLOSSARY.items()}


def _expand_with_glossary(tokens: set) -> set:
    expanded = set(tokens)
    for t in tokens:
        if t in FR_EN_GLOSSARY:
            expanded.add(FR_EN_GLOSSARY[t])
        if t in EN_FR_GLOSSARY:
            expanded.add(EN_FR_GLOSSARY[t])
    return expanded


# --- Offline machine translation (optional layer) ---------------------------

_translation_cache = {}
_mt_available = None

# Separate from _mt_available (which only tracks whether the argostranslate
# PACKAGE imports) — this tracks whether translation actually WORKS, i.e.
# whether the fr<->en language packages from setup_translation.py are
# actually installed on this machine. See is_translation_available() below
# for why this distinction matters.
_mt_health_checked = False
_mt_health_ok = False


def _get_translator():
    global _mt_available
    if _mt_available is False:
        return None
    try:
        import argostranslate.translate
        _mt_available = True
        return argostranslate.translate
    except ImportError:
        _mt_available = False
        return None


def _mt_translate(text: str, from_code: str, to_code: str) -> str:
    """Returns translated text, or the ORIGINAL text unchanged if MT is
    unavailable/uninstalled/fails — never raises, never blocks matching.
    """
    if not text:
        return ""
    cache_key = (text, from_code, to_code)
    if cache_key in _translation_cache:
        return _translation_cache[cache_key]

    translate_mod = _get_translator()
    if translate_mod is None:
        return text

    try:
        result = translate_mod.translate(text, from_code, to_code)
    except Exception:
        result = text

    _translation_cache[cache_key] = result
    return result


def is_translation_available() -> bool:
    """Actively verifies the offline MT layer can really translate a word —
    not just that the argostranslate PACKAGE imports successfully.

    Confirmed real failure mode: argostranslate==1.9.6 (from
    requirements.txt) installs and imports cleanly, so _get_translator()
    happily returns the module — but the two .argosmodel language packages
    (Language/translate-en_fr-1_9.argosmodel and translate-fr_en-1_9)
    listed in scripts/setup_translation.py are a SEPARATE manual
    installation step. If that step was never run on a given machine,
    every real translate() call raises internally, which _mt_translate()
    deliberately swallows via a broad `except Exception` (so matching never
    crashes) — but that also means cross-lingual matching silently
    degrades to glossary-only with NO visible sign anything is wrong.
    Call this once (e.g. at app/reconciliation startup) to surface that
    state instead of discovering it later as an unexplained run of
    'translated_candidate' matches that never actually fire.

    Cached after the first real check: translate() either works or it
    doesn't for the lifetime of this process, so re-attempting it on every
    reconcile() call would be wasted work for no new information.
    """
    global _mt_health_checked, _mt_health_ok
    if _mt_health_checked:
        return _mt_health_ok

    _mt_health_checked = True
    translate_mod = _get_translator()

    if translate_mod is None:
        logger.warning(
            "Cross-lingual matching: argostranslate is not installed — "
            "cross_lingual_similarity() will fall back to the curated "
            "glossary only. Run: pip install argostranslate"
        )
        _mt_health_ok = False
        return False

    try:
        # "BOBINE" is deliberately a word ALSO in the curated glossary, so
        # a working MT engine and a non-working one are both able to
        # return *a* result here — the real test is whether the engine
        # itself produced it (i.e. didn't just error out internally).
        result = translate_mod.translate("BOBINE", "fr", "en")
        _mt_health_ok = bool(result) and result.strip() != ""
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning(
            "Cross-lingual matching: argostranslate is installed but a "
            "test translation failed (%s) — the fr<->en language packages "
            "are most likely not installed. Run "
            "backend/scripts/setup_translation.py with the .argosmodel "
            "files in backend/Language/. Falling back to the curated "
            "glossary only in the meantime.", exc,
        )
        _mt_health_ok = False

    return _mt_health_ok


def cross_lingual_similarity(name_a: str, name_b: str) -> float:
    """Combines the curated glossary (precise, known terms) with offline MT
    (automatic, everything else). Either one finding real token overlap is
    enough. Falls back gracefully to glossary-only if argos-translate isn't
    installed/set up yet — this function never fails outright.
    """
    tokens_a = _expand_with_glossary(normalize_and_tokenize(name_a))
    tokens_b = _expand_with_glossary(normalize_and_tokenize(name_b))

    tokens_a |= normalize_and_tokenize(_mt_translate(name_a, "fr", "en"))
    tokens_a |= normalize_and_tokenize(_mt_translate(name_a, "en", "fr"))
    tokens_b |= normalize_and_tokenize(_mt_translate(name_b, "fr", "en"))
    tokens_b |= normalize_and_tokenize(_mt_translate(name_b, "en", "fr"))

    if not tokens_a or not tokens_b:
        return 0.0
    intersection = tokens_a & tokens_b
    union = tokens_a | tokens_b
    return len(intersection) / len(union)




================================================================================
FILE: backend\studio\reconcile\reconciler.py
================================================================================

"""
Matches a STEP-derived BOM against an MBOM/APL, producing a
confidence-scored reconciliation. Every rule here was derived from an
actual reconciliation run against real Safran APL + STEP file pairs.
"""

import re
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
from .mbom_loader import strip_hierarchy_dots, get_hierarchy_depth
from .nomenclature import token_similarity, cross_lingual_similarity, component_type_match
from .structural_context import (
    build_mbom_parent_map, build_step_parent_map,
    structural_match_score, is_nested_under_another_candidate,
)



# --- Part number normalization ---------------------------------------------

def _clean_pn_common(pn: str) -> str:
    """Cleanup applied symmetrically to both STEP and MBOM part numbers."""
    # Confirmed real case: STEP part number 'F6137-M83461/1-142 (AS5857)'
    # carries a trailing CATIA-added parenthetical annotation that never
    # appears in the MBOM at all — stripping it is what turns this into a
    # genuine exact match (MBOM's real row is plain 'M83461-1-142').
    pn = re.sub(r"\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$", "", pn)
    pn = pn.replace("/", "-")
    # Deliberate trailing-suffix stripping FIRST (instance/config markers,
    # e.g. "_L0", "_01") — these are specific, known patterns.
    pn = re.sub(r"_L\d+$", "", pn, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    pn = re.sub(r"_\d+$", "", pn)
    # THEN a blanket underscore->dash pass for anything left over.
    # Confirmed real case: 'M83461_1-019' uses an underscore as a plain
    # separator mid-string (not a trailing suffix pattern), which the
    # rules above never touch — this catches that without disturbing the
    # deliberate suffix-stripping above, since those cases are already
    # handled and removed by the time this runs.
    pn = pn.replace("_", "-")
    return pn.strip()


def normalize_part_number(part_number: str, manuf_prefix: str = None,
                           root_product_number: str = None) -> str:
    pn = part_number.strip()
    if manuf_prefix and pn.upper().startswith(manuf_prefix.upper() + "-"):
        pn = pn[len(manuf_prefix) + 1:]
    pn, _ = strip_hierarchy_dots(pn)
    if root_product_number:
        suffix = f"-{root_product_number.strip().upper()}"
        if pn.upper().endswith(suffix):
            pn = pn[: -len(suffix)]
    return _clean_pn_common(pn)


def normalize_mbom_part_number(part_number: str) -> str:
    pn, _ = strip_hierarchy_dots(part_number.strip())
    return _clean_pn_common(pn)


def detect_dominant_prefix(step_bom: list) -> str:
    from collections import Counter
    prefixes = [item.get("partNumber", "").split("-", 1)[0].upper()
                for item in step_bom if "-" in item.get("partNumber", "")]
    if not prefixes:
        return None
    most_common_prefix, count = Counter(prefixes).most_common(1)[0]
    return most_common_prefix if count / len(prefixes) >= 0.5 else None

def resolve_trailing_letter_variants(unmatched_step, matched_by_key, manuf_prefix, root_product_number):
    """Post-processing pass, run after everything else. For items still
    unmatched after all tiers, checks whether stripping a single trailing
    letter from their normalized part number matches an ALREADY-matched
    item's key — and only merges if the resulting SUMMED quantity exactly
    equals what MBOM declares for that part.

    Confirmed real case: 'M83461-1-014_L0' (qty 1, matched to MBOM's
    'M83461-1-014' which declares qty 3) and 'M83461/1-014A' (qty 2,
    otherwise unmatched) sum to exactly 3.

    Deliberately requires exact quantity verification before merging —
    the earlier near-duplicate-typo tier merged purely on string
    proximity with no such check and caused a real false merge between
    two unrelated parts. This is both narrower (one trailing letter only,
    not a broad search) and safer (the sum must independently verify).
    """
    resolved_indices = []
    for idx, u in enumerate(unmatched_step):
        norm = normalize_part_number(u.step_part_number, manuf_prefix, root_product_number)
        if not norm or not norm[-1].isalpha():
            continue
        stripped_key = norm[:-1].rstrip("-").upper()
        if stripped_key in matched_by_key:
            existing = matched_by_key[stripped_key]
            if existing.mbom_qty is None:
                continue
            candidate_total = existing.step_qty + u.step_qty
            if candidate_total == existing.mbom_qty:
                existing.step_qty = candidate_total
                existing.member_part_numbers.append(u.step_part_number)
                existing.quantity_match = True
                existing.flags.append(
                    f"Resolved via trailing-letter variant: '{u.step_part_number}' (qty {u.step_qty}) "
                    f"summed with the existing match on '{stripped_key}' — combined total "
                    f"{candidate_total} matches MBOM's declared qty {existing.mbom_qty} exactly. "
                    f"Verify this is genuinely the same part before fully trusting."
                )
                resolved_indices.append(idx)
    for idx in sorted(resolved_indices, reverse=True):
        del unmatched_step[idx]
    return unmatched_step

# --- Part-number edit distance (typo detection) -----------------------------

def levenshtein(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """Small, dependency-free edit distance — these are short part number
    strings, no need for a library. Confirmed real case: STEP part number
    'M83641/1-009' is a single digit-transposition typo away from the
    real MBOM part 'M83461-1-009' — nomenclature-only matching missed
    this entirely and guessed a wrong, unrelated part instead.
    """
    if a == b:
        return 0
    prev = list(range(len(b) + 1))
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        curr = [i] + [0] * len(b)
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            cost = 0 if ca == cb else 1
            curr[j] = min(prev[j] + 1, curr[j-1] + 1, prev[j-1] + cost)
        prev = curr
    return prev[-1]


def find_near_duplicate_part_number(norm_pn: str, mbom_by_pn: dict, used_mbom_keys: set,
                                     max_distance: int = 2) -> tuple:
    """Returns (mbom_rec, distance) for the closest near-identical MBOM
    part number within max_distance edits, or (None, None). Deliberately
    checked BEFORE nomenclature-only fuzzy matching — a near-identical
    part number is a much stronger, more specific signal than generic
    nomenclature overlap, and should win over it.
    """
    best_rec, best_dist = None, max_distance + 1
    for pn_key, rec in mbom_by_pn.items():
        if pn_key in used_mbom_keys or is_likely_process_spec(rec):
            continue
        if abs(len(pn_key) - len(norm_pn)) > max_distance:
            continue
        dist = levenshtein(norm_pn.upper(), pn_key)
        if 0 < dist <= max_distance and dist < best_dist:
            best_rec, best_dist = rec, dist
    return (best_rec, best_dist) if best_rec else (None, None)


# --- Placeholder detection --------------------------------------------------

PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS = [
    re.compile(r"^TEST\d*$", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"^TBD$", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"^PLACEHOLDER$", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"^XXX+$", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"^\d{1,3}$"),
]


def is_placeholder_part_number(part_number: str) -> bool:
    pn = part_number.strip()
    return any(p.match(pn) for p in PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS)


# --- Supersession parsing ---------------------------------------------------

SUPERSESSION_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"\{?\s*([A-Z0-9\-\.]+)\s*/\s*"
    r"(REMPLACE|EST UNE EVOLUTION DE)\s*\([^)]*\)\s*/\s*"
    r"([A-Z0-9\-\.]+)\s*\}?",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def parse_supersession(comments: str) -> dict:
    if not comments:
        return None
    m = SUPERSESSION_PATTERN.search(comments)
    if not m:
        return None
    referenced_pn, relation, other_pn = m.groups()
    return {
        "referenced_part_number": referenced_pn.strip(),
        "other_part_number": other_pn.strip(),
        "relation": relation.strip().upper(),
    }


def build_supersession_index(mbom_records: list) -> dict:
    index = {}
    for rec in mbom_records:
        sup = parse_supersession(rec.get("comments", ""))
        if sup:
            index[sup["referenced_part_number"].upper()] = rec
            index[sup["other_part_number"].upper()] = rec
    return index


# --- Process-spec filtering --------------------------------------------------

NON_PHYSICAL_PART_PREFIXES = ("NCT", "IFC", "PCS-")


def is_likely_process_spec(mbom_record: dict) -> bool:
    pn = mbom_record.get("part_number", "").lstrip(".").upper()
    return pn.startswith(NON_PHYSICAL_PART_PREFIXES)


# --- Multi-row MBOM aggregation ---------------------------------------------

def build_mbom_by_pn_grouped(mbom_records: list) -> dict:
    """Groups ALL MBOM rows sharing the same normalized part number (not
    just the last one seen). Confirmed real case: 'EQ8734-004' appears as
    two separate rows (qty 2 + qty 1) at different assembly positions,
    summing to exactly the STEP-found total of 3 — comparing against only
    one row was the actual cause of that mismatch, not a real
    discrepancy.
    """
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for rec in mbom_records:
        clean = normalize_mbom_part_number(rec.get("part_number", ""))
        groups[clean.upper()].append(rec)
    return dict(groups)


def summed_qty(records: list) -> int:
    total, any_valid = 0, False
    for rec in records:
        qty_raw = rec.get("qty", "")
        try:
            total += int(float(qty_raw)) if qty_raw != "" else 0
            any_valid = True
        except ValueError:
            pass
    return total if any_valid else None

def find_embedded_part_number(norm_pn: str, mbom_by_pn: dict, used_mbom_keys: set):
    """Checks whether norm_pn CONTAINS a real MBOM part number as a
    contiguous dash-separated token subsequence — e.g. 'GD69046-REP'
    contains 'GD69046'; 'FILS-BOBINES-GD69041' contains 'GD69041' as its
    last token, regardless of position (prefix, suffix, or middle).

    Confirmed real need: the general weighted last-resort scorer picks
    the WRONG candidate for cases like this — generic semantic/structural
    signals from an unrelated but similarly-described part (e.g.
    'ROTOR RECTIFIE' pulling toward 'EQUIPPED GROUND ROTOR' instead of the
    real match 'ROTOR SHAFT') outweigh a much stronger, highly specific
    part-number correspondence. This checks that correspondence directly,
    as its own dedicated signal, instead of diluting it into an average.
    No hardcoded suffix/prefix patterns — works for any decoration as
    long as the real part number survives as a clean dash-token.
    """
    parts = norm_pn.upper().split("-")
    for i in range(len(parts)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(parts) + 1):
            candidate = "-".join(parts[i:j])
            if candidate == norm_pn.upper():
                continue  # the whole string — that's Tier 1's job, not this
            if candidate in mbom_by_pn and candidate not in used_mbom_keys and not is_likely_process_spec(mbom_by_pn[candidate]):
                return mbom_by_pn[candidate], candidate
    return None, None

# --- Variant groups (J/K style interchangeable options) ---------------------

def build_variant_groups(mbom_records: list, mbom_parent_map: dict) -> dict:
    """Groups MBOM rows sharing the same (parent, Seq. Number) into
    'variant slots'. Confirmed real bug: grouping by seq_number ALONE is
    wrong — 'Seq. No.' resets/repeats independently under each parent
    assembly in this report format, so unrelated rows under DIFFERENT
    parents that happen to share the same local seq number string were
    being incorrectly treated as interchangeable variants of each other.
    Confirmed real case: MS21209F4-15/NAS1130-4FL15 (seq '200', under
    parent GD69029) and MS21209F4-20/NAS1130-4FL20 (seq '200', under
    parent GD69030) are two DIFFERENT variant slots in two different
    sub-assemblies that only coincidentally share the same seq number.
    """
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for rec in mbom_records:
        if is_likely_process_spec(rec):
            continue
        seq = rec.get("seq_number")
        if not seq:
            continue
        own_pn = strip_hierarchy_dots(rec.get("part_number", ""))[0].upper()
        parent = mbom_parent_map.get(own_pn)
        groups[(parent, seq)].append(rec)
    return {k: recs for k, recs in groups.items() if len(recs) > 1}


def variant_siblings_for(mbom_rec: dict, variant_groups: dict, mbom_parent_map: dict) -> list:
    seq = mbom_rec.get("seq_number")
    if not seq:
        return []
    own_pn = strip_hierarchy_dots(mbom_rec.get("part_number", ""))[0].upper()
    parent = mbom_parent_map.get(own_pn)
    key = (parent, seq)
    if key not in variant_groups:
        return []
    siblings = []
    for rec in variant_groups[key]:
        rec_pn = strip_hierarchy_dots(rec.get("part_number", ""))[0]
        if rec_pn.upper() == own_pn:
            continue
        qty_raw = rec.get("qty", "")
        try:
            qty = int(float(qty_raw)) if qty_raw != "" else None
        except ValueError:
            qty = None
        siblings.append({
            "equiv": rec.get("equiv"), "part_number": rec_pn,
            "description": rec.get("description"), "qty": qty,
        })
    return siblings

def effective_quantity(pn_upper: str, mbom_by_pn_grouped: dict, variant_groups: dict,
                        mbom_parent_map: dict, _visiting: set = None) -> int:
    """Resolves a part's REAL, usable quantity — not just its raw declared
    qty. If a part's own declared qty is 0 but it has a variant sibling
    with a nonzero qty (the J/K pattern), returns the sibling's qty
    instead. This is what makes ancestor-multiplication safe: multiplying
    by a raw qty=0 "inactive variant" ancestor produces a nonsensical 0,
    but resolving to the ancestor's actually-active sibling first gives a
    real, usable multiplier.
    """
    _visiting = _visiting or set()
    if pn_upper in _visiting:
        return 1  # guard against any pathological cycle
    _visiting.add(pn_upper)

    records = mbom_by_pn_grouped.get(pn_upper)
    if not records:
        return 1
    qty = summed_qty(records)
    if qty:
        return qty

    # Own quantity is 0/unknown — check variant siblings at the same slot.
    for rec in records:
        for sib in variant_siblings_for(rec, variant_groups, mbom_parent_map):
            sib_pn = strip_hierarchy_dots(sib["part_number"])[0].upper()
            if sib.get("qty"):
                return sib["qty"]
    return qty or 1


def ancestor_multiplier(pn_upper: str, mbom_parent_map: dict, mbom_by_pn_grouped: dict,
                         variant_groups: dict, max_depth: int = 15) -> int:
    """Product of the EFFECTIVE quantity of every ancestor up the MBOM
    hierarchy (not counting the part's own row, which is compared
    separately). Confirmed real case: '41320677006' has parent
    'MS21209F0615' with MBOM qty 11 — 1(own) x 11(ancestor) = 11, matching
    STEP's found total of 11 exactly.
    """
    product = 1
    current = mbom_parent_map.get(pn_upper)
    depth = 0
    while current and depth < max_depth:
        product *= effective_quantity(current, mbom_by_pn_grouped, variant_groups, mbom_parent_map)
        current = mbom_parent_map.get(current)
        depth += 1
    return product

# --- Result structure --------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class MatchResult:
    step_part_number: str
    step_name: str
    step_qty: int
    status: str
    confidence: float
    mbom_part_number: str = None
    mbom_description: str = None
    mbom_qty: int = None
    mbom_manuf_code: str = None
    mbom_level: int = None
    quantity_match: bool = None
    flags: list = field(default_factory=list)
    candidates: list = field(default_factory=list)
    signals: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    variant_siblings: list = field(default_factory=list)
    effectivity_code: str = None
    member_part_numbers: list = field(default_factory=list)


WEIGHTS = {
    "structural": 0.30, "semantic": 0.25, "component_type": 0.20,
    "qty": 0.10, "spec": 0.10, "part_number_sim": 0.05,
}
AI_SEMANTIC_WEIGHT = 0.20


def spec_match_score(step_material, mbom_material_spec):
    if not step_material or not mbom_material_spec:
        return 0.0
    return token_similarity(step_material, mbom_material_spec)

def group_step_bom(step_bom: list, manuf_prefix: str = None, root_product_number: str = None) -> list:
    """Groups STEP items that normalize to the same part number, summing
    their instance counts before matching. Confirmed real case:
    'M83461_1-019' and 'M83461/1-019_L1' are two separate STEP leaf
    entries (each instances=1) representing the same nominal MBOM part
    'M83461-1-019' (qty 2) — comparing each individually produced two
    false '1 != 2' mismatches; combined, they correctly sum to 2 == 2.
    """
    groups = {}
    for item in step_bom:
        # .get(key, "") only falls back when the KEY is absent — if the
        # JSON has "partNumber": null explicitly (real case: parts where
        # the C++ tool's entity lookup never resolved a name), .get()
        # still returns None and crashes downstream on the first
        # .strip() call. `or ""` catches both missing-key AND
        # explicit-None uniformly.
        item_pn = item.get("partNumber") or ""
        item_name = item.get("name") or ""

        norm_pn = normalize_part_number(item_pn, manuf_prefix, root_product_number)
        key = norm_pn.upper()
        if key not in groups:
            groups[key] = {
                "partNumber": item_pn,
                "name": item_name,
                "material": item.get("material"),
                "instances": 0,
                "_member_part_numbers": [],
            }
        groups[key]["instances"] += item.get("instances", 1)
        groups[key]["_member_part_numbers"].append(item_pn)
    return list(groups.values())


def score_candidate(step_qty, step_part_number, step_name, step_material, norm_step_pn,
                     step_parent_map, mbom_rec, mbom_parent_map, mbom_records_by_pn,
                     semantic_scorer=None):
    mbom_pn = strip_hierarchy_dots(mbom_rec.get("part_number", ""))[0]
    mbom_qty_raw = mbom_rec.get("qty", "")
    try:
        mbom_qty = int(float(mbom_qty_raw)) if mbom_qty_raw != "" else None
    except ValueError:
        mbom_qty = None

    signals = {
        "structural": structural_match_score(step_part_number, step_parent_map, mbom_pn, mbom_parent_map, mbom_records_by_pn),
        "semantic": token_similarity(step_name, mbom_rec.get("description", "")),
        "component_type": component_type_match(step_name, mbom_rec.get("description", "")),
        "qty": 1.0 if (mbom_qty is not None and mbom_qty == step_qty) else 0.0,
        "spec": spec_match_score(step_material, mbom_rec.get("material_spec", "")),
        "part_number_sim": SequenceMatcher(None, norm_step_pn.upper(), mbom_pn.upper()).ratio(),
    }

    weights = dict(WEIGHTS)
    if semantic_scorer is not None:
        signals["ai_semantic"] = semantic_scorer(step_name, mbom_rec.get("description", ""))
        weights = {k: v * (1 - AI_SEMANTIC_WEIGHT) for k, v in weights.items()}
        weights["ai_semantic"] = AI_SEMANTIC_WEIGHT

    combined = sum(signals[k] * weights[k] for k in signals)
    return combined, signals


def format_candidate_note(mbom_rec, score, signals):
    mbom_pn = strip_hierarchy_dots(mbom_rec.get("part_number", ""))[0]
    sig_str = " ".join(f"{k}:{v:.2f}" for k, v in signals.items())
    return f"{mbom_pn} ({mbom_rec.get('description','')}, {sig_str}, score={score:.2f})"


def reconcile(step_bom, mbom_records, manuf_prefix=None, root_product_number=None,
              fuzzy_threshold=0.85, fuzzy_ambiguity_margin=0.1, assembly_tree=None,
              semantic_scorer=None, cross_lingual_threshold=0.5, expected_variant=None,
              step_shape_descriptors=None, sibling_nomenclature_threshold=0.5,
              part_number_max_edit_distance=2):
    """
    sibling_nomenclature_threshold: raised from 0.3 to 0.5 — confirmed
        real false positives at 0.3-0.33 where a single shared GENERIC
        component-type word (e.g. "RING", "INSERT") alone cleared the old
        bar, incorrectly flagging unrelated parts as "same branch,
        related nomenclature" siblings.
    """
    if manuf_prefix is None:
        manuf_prefix = detect_dominant_prefix(step_bom)

    step_bom = group_step_bom(step_bom, manuf_prefix, root_product_number)

    mbom_by_pn_grouped = build_mbom_by_pn_grouped(mbom_records)
    mbom_by_pn = {k: v[0] for k, v in mbom_by_pn_grouped.items()}  # representative record per key, for description/level/etc.

    supersession_index = build_supersession_index(mbom_records)
    mbom_parent_map = build_mbom_parent_map(mbom_records)
    step_parent_map = build_step_parent_map(assembly_tree) if assembly_tree else {}
    variant_groups = build_variant_groups(mbom_records, mbom_parent_map)

    matched, unmatched_step = [], []
    used_mbom_keys = set()
    matched_by_key = {}  # matched_key -> MatchResult, for the merge-on-typo-match logic above

    for step_item in step_bom:
        step_pn_raw = step_item.get("partNumber", "")
        step_name = step_item.get("name", "")
        step_qty = step_item.get("instances", 1)
        step_material = (step_item.get("material") or {}).get("name", "")
        member_pns = step_item.get("_member_part_numbers", [step_pn_raw])

        norm_pn = normalize_part_number(step_pn_raw, manuf_prefix, root_product_number)
        mbom_rec = mbom_by_pn.get(norm_pn.upper())
        status, confidence, flags, candidates = "matched", 1.0, [], []
        matched_key = norm_pn.upper() if mbom_rec else None

        if mbom_rec is not None:
            own_pn = strip_hierarchy_dots(mbom_rec.get("part_number", ""))[0].upper()
            for pn_key, rec in mbom_by_pn.items():
                if pn_key == own_pn or is_likely_process_spec(rec):
                    continue
                rec_qty_raw = rec.get("qty", "")
                try:
                    rec_qty = int(float(rec_qty_raw)) if rec_qty_raw != "" else None
                except ValueError:
                    rec_qty = None
                same_qty = rec_qty == step_qty
                same_branch = mbom_parent_map.get(pn_key) == mbom_parent_map.get(own_pn)
                nomenclature_related = token_similarity(step_name, rec.get("description", "")) >= sibling_nomenclature_threshold
                rec_equiv = (rec.get("equiv") or "").strip().upper()
                is_different_variant = (expected_variant is not None and rec_equiv and rec_equiv != expected_variant.strip().upper())

                if same_qty and same_branch and nomenclature_related:
                    if is_different_variant:
                        flags.append(f"Note: '{rec.get('part_number')}' (equiv '{rec.get('equiv')}') is a different variant than expected '{expected_variant}' — likely fine as-is.")
                    else:
                        flags.append(f"Exact match found on '{mbom_rec.get('part_number')}', but '{rec.get('part_number')}' ({rec.get('description')}) sits in the same assembly branch with matching quantity ({step_qty}) and related nomenclature — verify which part number is currently active.")
                        candidates.append({"mbom_part_number": strip_hierarchy_dots(rec.get("part_number", ""))[0], "description": rec.get("description"), "qty": rec_qty, "level": get_hierarchy_depth(rec), "reason": "same branch, matching quantity, related nomenclature, different part number"})

        # Tier 2: supersession
        if mbom_rec is None:
            sup_rec = supersession_index.get(norm_pn.upper())
            if sup_rec:
                mbom_rec = sup_rec
                status = "matched_via_supersession"
                confidence = 0.9
                matched_key = strip_hierarchy_dots(sup_rec.get("part_number", ""))[0].upper()
                flags.append(f"STEP part number '{norm_pn}' is superseded in MBOM by '{sup_rec.get('part_number')}'.")

        if is_placeholder_part_number(norm_pn):
            flags.append(f"STEP part number '{step_pn_raw}' matches a known placeholder pattern.")
            if mbom_rec is None:
                status, confidence = "placeholder_suspected", 0.0

        # Tier 2.5: near-identical part number (typo detection).
        # Finds the closest candidate WITHOUT excluding already-used keys
        # first — confirmed real case: 'M83461-1-014A' is genuinely
        # closest to 'M83461-1-014' (distance 1), but that row was
        # already consumed by a separate exact match, and excluding it
        # outright caused a worse, wrong fallback ('M83461-1-142',
        # distance 2) to be picked instead. If the true closest candidate
        # is already matched, this merges into that existing result's
        # instance count (same logic as STEP-side grouping above) rather
        # than either blocking it or accepting a worse guess.
        #
        # Deliberately does NOT decide FOR you whether a trailing-letter
        # difference means "same part, extra instance" or "genuinely
        # distinct authorized variant" — aerospace part numbering uses
        # both conventions in real files. This surfaces the closest
        # candidate and flags it for confirmation either way, rather than
        # silently guessing.
        if mbom_rec is None:
            near_rec, dist = find_near_duplicate_part_number(
                norm_pn, mbom_by_pn, set(), part_number_max_edit_distance  # no used-key exclusion here
            )
            if near_rec is not None:
                near_key = strip_hierarchy_dots(near_rec.get("part_number", ""))[0].upper()
                if near_key not in used_mbom_keys:
                    mbom_rec = near_rec
                    status = "fuzzy_candidate"
                    confidence = round(1.0 - (dist / max(len(norm_pn), 1)) * 0.5, 2)
                    matched_key = near_key
                    flags.append(
                        f"Part number '{step_pn_raw}' is {dist} character(s) different from MBOM's "
                        f"'{near_rec.get('part_number')}' — could be the same part with a typo, or a "
                        f"genuinely distinct variant. Verify before trusting."
                    )

        # Tier 2.6: embedded real part number, verified by exact quantity
        # agreement. Confirmed real cases: STEP decorates a genuinely
        # correct part number with extra prefix/suffix text ('GD69046-REP',
        # 'FILS-BOBINES-GD69041') that a diluted weighted-average score
        # gets wrong, but which resolves cleanly and confidently once
        # checked directly and confirmed against the real declared quantity.
        if mbom_rec is None:
            embedded_rec, embedded_key = find_embedded_part_number(norm_pn, mbom_by_pn, used_mbom_keys)
            if embedded_rec is not None:
                embedded_qty_raw = embedded_rec.get("qty", "")
                try:
                    embedded_qty = int(float(embedded_qty_raw)) if embedded_qty_raw != "" else None
                except ValueError:
                    embedded_qty = None
                if embedded_qty is not None and embedded_qty == step_qty:
                    mbom_rec = embedded_rec
                    status = "fuzzy_candidate"
                    confidence = 0.75
                    matched_key = embedded_key
                    flags.append(
                        f"STEP part number '{step_pn_raw}' contains real MBOM part '{embedded_key}' "
                        f"as an embedded token, with matching quantity ({step_qty}) confirming the "
                        f"correspondence. The surrounding text ('{step_pn_raw}') may indicate a "
                        f"specific lifecycle state or sub-reference — verify before fully trusting."
                    )


        # Tier 3: nomenclature-gated fuzzy
        if mbom_rec is None:
            pool = [(k, r) for k, r in mbom_by_pn.items() if k not in used_mbom_keys and not is_likely_process_spec(r) and token_similarity(step_name, r.get("description", "")) >= fuzzy_threshold]
            pool_pns = [k for k, _ in pool]
            pool = [(k, r) for k, r in pool if not is_nested_under_another_candidate(k, pool_pns, mbom_parent_map)]
            scored = []
            for k, r in pool:
                combined, signals = score_candidate(step_qty, step_pn_raw, step_name, step_material, norm_pn, step_parent_map, r, mbom_parent_map, mbom_by_pn, semantic_scorer)
                scored.append((combined, r, signals, k))
            scored.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])

            if len(scored) == 1 or (len(scored) > 1 and scored[0][0] - scored[1][0] >= fuzzy_ambiguity_margin):
                best_score, best_rec, best_signals, best_key = scored[0]
                mbom_rec, status, confidence, matched_key = best_rec, "fuzzy_candidate", round(best_score, 2), best_key
                flags.append(f"No part-number match — best candidate is {format_candidate_note(best_rec, best_score, best_signals)}.")
            elif len(scored) > 1:
                ranked_notes = "; ".join(format_candidate_note(r, s, sig) for s, r, sig, _ in scored[:4])
                ranked_candidates = [{"mbom_part_number": strip_hierarchy_dots(r.get("part_number", ""))[0], "description": r.get("description"), "score": round(s, 2), "level": get_hierarchy_depth(r), "signals": {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in sig.items()}} for s, r, sig, _ in scored[:4]]
                unmatched_step.append(MatchResult(step_part_number=step_pn_raw, step_name=step_name, step_qty=step_qty, status="ambiguous", confidence=0.0, flags=[f"Multiple candidates too close: {ranked_notes}."], candidates=ranked_candidates))
                continue

        # Tier 4: cross-lingual
        if mbom_rec is None:
            cross_pool = [(k, r) for k, r in mbom_by_pn.items() if k not in used_mbom_keys and not is_likely_process_spec(r) and cross_lingual_similarity(step_name, r.get("description", "")) >= cross_lingual_threshold]
            cross_pool_pns = [k for k, _ in cross_pool]
            cross_pool = [(k, r) for k, r in cross_pool if not is_nested_under_another_candidate(k, cross_pool_pns, mbom_parent_map)]
            cross_scored = []
            for k, r in cross_pool:
                combined, signals = score_candidate(step_qty, step_pn_raw, step_name, step_material, norm_pn, step_parent_map, r, mbom_parent_map, mbom_by_pn, semantic_scorer)
                signals["cross_lingual"] = round(cross_lingual_similarity(step_name, r.get("description", "")), 2)
                cross_scored.append((combined, r, signals, k))
            cross_scored.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])
            if cross_scored and (len(cross_scored) == 1 or cross_scored[0][0] - cross_scored[1][0] >= fuzzy_ambiguity_margin):
                best_score, best_rec, best_signals, best_key = cross_scored[0]
                mbom_rec, status, confidence, matched_key = best_rec, "translated_candidate", round(best_score * 0.75, 2), best_key
                flags.append(f"Cross-language candidate — {format_candidate_note(best_rec, best_score, best_signals)}.")

        # Tier 5: last-resort weighted structural/semantic match. Confirmed
        # real case: STEP 'D56700-0331' ("COMPRESSION SPRING - DYNAMIC")
        # has NO corresponding part number anywhere in the MBOM at all
        # (independently verified against the raw STEP entity graph — this
        # is a real, confirmed assembly child of the root, not a text
        # coincidence) — and its nomenclature overlap with the true match
        # ('SPRING') is too weak (0.33) to clear Tiers 3/4's thresholds.
        # This tier removes the nomenclature gate entirely and scores
        # EVERY remaining candidate on the full weighted signal set
        # (structural/semantic/component-type/qty/spec/part-number),
        # accepting only when the top candidate has a clear, wide margin
        # over the next-best — deliberately the most conservative tier,
        # since it's the last thing tried before giving up.
        if mbom_rec is None:
            last_resort_pool = [
                (k, r) for k, r in mbom_by_pn.items()
                if k not in used_mbom_keys and not is_likely_process_spec(r)
            ]
            last_resort_scored = []
            for k, r in last_resort_pool:
                combined, signals = score_candidate(
                    step_qty, step_pn_raw, step_name, step_material, norm_pn,
                    step_parent_map, r, mbom_parent_map, mbom_by_pn, semantic_scorer,
                )
                last_resort_scored.append((combined, r, signals, k))
            last_resort_scored.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])

            if last_resort_scored:
                best_score, best_rec, best_signals, best_key = last_resort_scored[0]
                second_score = last_resort_scored[1][0] if len(last_resort_scored) > 1 else 0.0
                clear_margin = best_score - second_score >= 0.15
                qty_agrees = best_signals.get("qty", 0.0) == 1.0
                if best_score >= 0.45 and clear_margin and qty_agrees:
                    mbom_rec = best_rec
                    status = "last_resort_candidate"
                    confidence = round(best_score * 0.6, 2)
                    matched_key = best_key
                    flags.append(
                        f"No part number, nomenclature, or cross-language match found. Best "
                        f"structural/semantic candidate (last resort): "
                        f"{format_candidate_note(best_rec, best_score, best_signals)}, margin over "
                        f"next-best: {best_score - second_score:.2f}. Requires manual confirmation "
                        f"before trusting — this is the least certain match tier."
                    )

        # Tier 6: shape-based suggestion, geometry only, no text signal at
        # all. Self-gated on corpus size — confirmed real case: with only
        # 20 confirmed corpus entries, the TRUE correct sibling for a
        # BACK-UP RING query ranked 4th of 5 nearest neighbors, not 1st.
        # Retrieval works mechanically at that size, but isn't reliably
        # RANKED yet. Stays dormant below the threshold rather than risk
        # confidently wrong suggestions, and activates automatically once
        # there's enough real confirmed data to trust — no manual
        # "turning it on" needed later.
        if mbom_rec is None and step_shape_descriptors is not None:
            from .shape_learning.corpus import corpus_size
            MIN_CORPUS_SIZE_FOR_SHAPE_MATCHING = 200
            if corpus_size() >= MIN_CORPUS_SIZE_FOR_SHAPE_MATCHING:
                from .shape_learning.retrieval import find_nearest
                query_desc = step_shape_descriptors.get(step_pn_raw)
                if query_desc is not None:
                    neighbors = find_nearest(query_desc, k=1)
                    if neighbors and neighbors[0]["distance"] < 1.0:
                        nb = neighbors[0]
                        nb_key = nb["part_number"].upper()
                        candidate = mbom_by_pn.get(nb_key)
                        if candidate and nb_key not in used_mbom_keys:
                            mbom_rec = candidate
                            status = "shape_suggested"
                            confidence = 0.3
                            matched_key = nb_key
                            flags.append(
                                f"No text-based match found at all. Closest shape match in the "
                                f"confirmed-parts corpus: '{nb['part_number']}' ({nb['description']}, "
                                f"distance {nb['distance']:.2f}). This is geometry-only evidence — "
                                f"requires manual confirmation."
                            )

        if mbom_rec is None:
            unmatched_step.append(MatchResult(step_part_number=step_pn_raw, step_name=step_name, step_qty=step_qty, status="unmatched", confidence=0.0, flags=["No corresponding MBOM line found."] + flags))
            continue

        final_score, final_signals = score_candidate(step_qty, step_pn_raw, step_name, step_material, norm_pn, step_parent_map, mbom_rec, mbom_parent_map, mbom_by_pn, semantic_scorer)
        if status in ("matched", "matched_via_supersession"):
            confidence = round(max(confidence, final_score), 2)

        used_mbom_keys.add(matched_key)

        # Quantity comparison now checks THREE things in order: (1) the
        # summed quantity across all MBOM rows sharing this part number,
        # (2) if that still doesn't match, whether multiplying by the
        # ancestor chain's effective quantity explains it, (3) if still
        # not, the existing variant-sibling check, (4) otherwise a real
        # flagged mismatch.
        grouped_records = mbom_by_pn_grouped.get(matched_key, [mbom_rec])
        mbom_qty = summed_qty(grouped_records)

        qty_match = (mbom_qty == step_qty) if mbom_qty is not None else None
        siblings, effectivity_code = [], None

        if qty_match is False:
            multiplier = ancestor_multiplier(matched_key, mbom_parent_map, mbom_by_pn_grouped, variant_groups)
            expected_with_multiplier = (mbom_qty or 0) * multiplier
            if multiplier > 1 and expected_with_multiplier == step_qty:
                qty_match = True
                flags.append(
                    f"Quantity resolved via parent-assembly multiplier: MBOM declares {mbom_qty} "
                    f"per parent instance, and the parent chain effectively installs this "
                    f"{multiplier}x — {mbom_qty} x {multiplier} = {step_qty}, matching STEP exactly."
                )
            else:
                group_siblings = variant_siblings_for(mbom_rec, variant_groups, mbom_parent_map)
                resolving_sibling = next((s for s in group_siblings if s.get("qty") == step_qty), None)
                if resolving_sibling:
                    qty_match = True
                    effectivity_code = resolving_sibling.get("equiv")
                    siblings = [resolving_sibling]
                    flags.append(f"Quantity resolved via variant match: STEP qty {step_qty} matches the '{resolving_sibling['equiv']}' variant ({resolving_sibling['part_number']}), not '{mbom_rec.get('equiv')}'.")
                elif group_siblings:
                    siblings = group_siblings
                    sibling_str = ", ".join(f"{s['equiv']} ({s['part_number']}, qty {s['qty']})" for s in group_siblings)
                    flags.append(f"Quantity mismatch: STEP has {step_qty}, MBOM has {mbom_qty} (equiv '{mbom_rec.get('equiv')}'). Checked alternates: {sibling_str} — none match.")
                else:
                    flags.append(f"Quantity mismatch: STEP has {step_qty}, MBOM has {mbom_qty}.")

        result_obj = MatchResult(
            step_part_number=step_pn_raw, step_name=step_name, step_qty=step_qty,
            status=status, confidence=confidence,
            mbom_part_number=strip_hierarchy_dots(mbom_rec.get("part_number", ""))[0],
            mbom_description=mbom_rec.get("description"), mbom_qty=mbom_qty,
            mbom_manuf_code=mbom_rec.get("manuf_code"), mbom_level=get_hierarchy_depth(mbom_rec),
            quantity_match=qty_match, flags=flags, candidates=candidates,
            signals={k: round(v, 2) for k, v in final_signals.items()},
            variant_siblings=siblings, effectivity_code=effectivity_code,
            member_part_numbers=member_pns,
        )
        matched.append(result_obj)
        matched_by_key[matched_key] = result_obj

    unmatched_step = resolve_trailing_letter_variants(unmatched_step, matched_by_key, manuf_prefix, root_product_number)
    unmatched_mbom = [
        {**rec, "level_depth": get_hierarchy_depth(rec)}
        for rec in mbom_records
        if strip_hierarchy_dots(rec.get("part_number", ""))[0].upper() not in used_mbom_keys
    ]

    return {"matched": matched, "unmatched_step": unmatched_step, "unmatched_mbom": unmatched_mbom}

FILE: backend\studio\reconcile\structural_context.py

"""
Reconstructs "who is this part's parent" on both sides of the reconciliation,
so structural position can be used as a matching signal — not just part
number and nomenclature.

Also derives EFFECTIVE (whole-top-assembly) quantities for MBOM lines by
multiplying down the hierarchy, since the raw Qty column on a multi-level
MBOM/APL is per-immediate-parent only, not a total (see
compute_effective_quantities below).

Confirmed real cases this addresses:
- MS21209F4-15, NAS1130-4FL15, and MS124694 all sit at the same MBOM level
  under the same parent (GD69029) — genuinely structural siblings, so
  structural matching alone won't disambiguate between them (quantity does).
- C72151 (level 1, direct child of the top assembly) vs EBC72151 (level 2,
  nested UNDER C72151 itself) are NOT structural siblings — EBC72151 is a
  sub-reference inside C72151's own branch, not a competing top-level
  candidate. This case IS resolved by structural filtering.
- A Safran APL (F6137-D24903000) has parts nested 3-5 levels deep with a
  qty > 1 at intermediate levels (e.g. WOUND STATOR under the top assembly
  qty=1, but its own child LAMINATION STACK holds 152 laminations, and a
  magnet 4 levels down is qty=3 per rotor while the rotor itself repeats).
  Comparing STEP's already-fully-multiplied instance count against that
  MBOM row's raw, un-multiplied qty produces false "quantity mismatch"
  flags on entirely correct parts. compute_effective_quantities fixes this.
"""

from .mbom_loader import strip_hierarchy_dots, get_hierarchy_depth

def build_mbom_parent_map(mbom_records: list) -> dict:
    """Returns {clean_part_number: parent_clean_part_number_or_None}.

    Reconstructed from row order + hierarchy depth via a simple stack:
    each row's parent is the nearest preceding row with a shallower depth.
    Depth comes from get_hierarchy_depth(), which handles both known
    conventions (leading dots on the part number, or a separate
    asterisk-based Niveau column).
    """
    parent_map = {}
    stack = []  # list of (depth, clean_part_number)

    for rec in mbom_records:
        pn = rec.get("part_number", "")
        clean, _ = strip_hierarchy_dots(pn)
        clean = clean.upper()
        depth = get_hierarchy_depth(rec)

        while stack and stack[-1][0] >= depth:
            stack.pop()

        parent_map[clean] = stack[-1][1] if stack else None
        stack.append((depth, clean))

    return parent_map


def _raw_qty(rec: dict):
    """Parses a single row's own Qty cell. Returns None if blank/non-numeric
    (distinct from 0, which is a real, meaningful value — e.g. a Find No.
    with qty 0 in a real APL meaning "not fitted on this variant")."""
    raw = rec.get("qty", "")
    try:
        return int(float(raw)) if raw != "" else None
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return None


def compute_effective_quantities(mbom_records: list, mbom_parent_map: dict) -> dict:
    """Returns {clean_part_number: effective_total_qty}.

    A multi-level MBOM/APL's Qty column is PER IMMEDIATE PARENT, not a
    total against the top assembly — e.g. "3 ea NORTH MAGNET" means 3 per
    rotor, and if that rotor itself only occurs once per top assembly the
    true total is 3, but if some ancestor further up also repeats (qty>1),
    the true total is 3 times THAT ancestor's own effective quantity too.

    This walks each part's ancestor chain (via mbom_parent_map, itself
    built in build_mbom_parent_map) from the part up to the root,
    multiplying every level's own raw qty together, so the result is the
    true count of that part needed to build ONE complete top assembly —
    directly comparable to a STEP/CAD converter's already-fully-multiplied
    "instances" count (see reconciler.py).

    A missing/non-numeric qty at any level (own row OR an ancestor) is
    treated as a multiplier of 1, not as "unknown"/aborting the chain.
    Confirmed real case: the top-level assembly row itself (Lev 0, e.g.
    D24903000) and several process/finish-spec rows have a BLANK Qty
    column entirely on this document, which conventionally means "one",
    not "not applicable" — silently bailing out on a blank ancestor qty
    would incorrectly discard the effective quantity of every part
    underneath it in the tree, which is the opposite of what's needed
    here (this function must always return a usable total).
    """
    own_qty = {}
    for rec in mbom_records:
        pn, _ = strip_hierarchy_dots(rec.get("part_number", ""))
        own_qty[pn.upper()] = _raw_qty(rec)

    effective = {}
    for pn in own_qty:
        total = 1
        current = pn
        depth_guard = 0
        while current and depth_guard < 30:  # guards against a corrupt/cyclic parent map
            q = own_qty.get(current)
            total *= q if q is not None else 1
            current = mbom_parent_map.get(current)
            depth_guard += 1
        effective[pn] = total

    return effective


def build_step_parent_map(assembly_tree: dict) -> dict:
    """Returns {step_part_number: nearest_ancestor_name}, walked from the
    converter's assembly_tree JSON. Uses the ancestor's NAME (e.g.
    'EQUIPED BODY') rather than its raw XCAF label id, since that's what's
    comparable against MBOM nomenclature — MBOM has no knowledge of STEP's
    internal label ids at all.

    Requires the part-level 'partNumber' field to be present on tree nodes
    matching the flat bom's partNumber (same converter output, so it is).
    """
    parent_map = {}

    def walk(node, ancestor_name):
        node_name = node.get("name")
        if node.get("isPart"):
            pn = node.get("partNumber")
            if pn:
                parent_map[pn] = ancestor_name
        for child in node.get("children", []):
            walk(child, node_name if not node.get("isPart") else ancestor_name)

    walk(assembly_tree, None)
    return parent_map


def structural_match_score(step_part_number: str, step_parent_map: dict,
                            mbom_candidate_pn: str, mbom_parent_map: dict,
                            mbom_records_by_pn: dict) -> float:
    """Returns 0.0-1.0. Compares the STEP part's ancestor NAME against the
    MBOM candidate's ancestor part number's nomenclature — fuzzy, since the
    two sides have no shared identifier for assembly-level containers
    (STEP has no MBOM part number for e.g. 'EQUIPED BODY', only a name).
    """
    from difflib import SequenceMatcher

    step_parent_name = step_parent_map.get(step_part_number)
    mbom_parent_pn = mbom_parent_map.get(mbom_candidate_pn.upper())

    if not step_parent_name or not mbom_parent_pn:
        return 0.0

    mbom_parent_rec = mbom_records_by_pn.get(mbom_parent_pn.upper())
    if not mbom_parent_rec:
        return 0.0

    mbom_parent_desc = mbom_parent_rec.get("description", "")
    return SequenceMatcher(None, step_parent_name.upper(), mbom_parent_desc.upper()).ratio()


def is_nested_under_another_candidate(candidate_pn: str, other_candidate_pns: list,
                                       mbom_parent_map: dict) -> bool:
    """True if candidate_pn's parent chain passes through another candidate
    in the same pool — i.e. it's a sub-reference nested inside a sibling
    candidate's own branch, not an independently competing match.

    Confirmed real case: EBC72151 is nested directly under C72151, and both
    appeared as tied candidates for the same STEP VALVE part. EBC72151
    should be excluded/demoted in favor of C72151 here.
    """
    current = mbom_parent_map.get(candidate_pn.upper())
    depth_guard = 0
    while current and depth_guard < 10:
        if current in {p.upper() for p in other_candidate_pns}:
            return True
        current = mbom_parent_map.get(current)
        depth_guard += 1
    return False

FILE: backend\studio\reconcile\shape_learning\backfill.py

"""
One-time (and re-runnable) script: mines PAST reconciliation results plus
their corresponding .glb files for confirmed matches, and populates the
shape corpus. Run manually:

    python -m shape_learning.backfill path/to/reconciliation_result.json path/to/model.glb
"""

import sys
import json
from .descriptors import extract_all_descriptors
from .corpus import add_entry, corpus_size


def backfill_from_result(result_path: str, glb_path: str):
    result = json.load(open(result_path))
    all_descriptors = extract_all_descriptors(glb_path)
    by_identity = {d["identity"]: d["descriptors"] for d in all_descriptors}

    added = 0
    for m in result.get("matched", []):
        if m["status"] not in ("matched", "manual"):
            continue  # only trust exact/manually-confirmed matches as training data
        identity = m["step_part_number"]
        descriptors = by_identity.get(identity)
        if descriptors is None:
            continue
        add_entry(
            part_number=m["mbom_part_number"],
            description=m.get("mbom_description", ""),
            descriptors=descriptors,
            source_file=glb_path,
            confidence_source=m["status"],
        )
        added += 1

    print(f"Added {added} entries. Corpus size now: {corpus_size()}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    backfill_from_result(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])

FILE: backend\studio\reconcile\shape_learning\corpus.py
